# M2 browser audits and keyword refresh

Enable browser audits by setting `RENDERER_URL=http://renderer:8080` in `.env`, then starting the stack with:

```sh
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml --env-file .env --profile renderer up -d --build
```

The audit form offers **Render JavaScript** and **Include Lighthouse lab scores**. Both default off. Rendered audits extract content and discover links from the browser DOM. A failed render produces a `render-failed` issue and retains the static HTML audit. Lighthouse scores, numeric lab metrics, measurement time and improvement suggestions are stored in `audit_pages.browser_result` (migration 0004) and displayed on the page detail screen. They are desktop lab measurements, not field Core Web Vitals. A Lighthouse failure is reported independently of successful DOM rendering.

The renderer runs one browser operation at a time, with a 90-second deadline, isolated browser state per request and a 1 MiB DOM limit. The Rust client waits for a busy renderer for up to roughly two minutes. Large audits with Lighthouse are substantially slower; start with a small page budget. Browser startup failure or an unavailable service is visible in page issues.

## Network boundary

The Chromium container is on an internal Docker network with no external route or published ports. Its HTTP/HTTPS traffic goes through `renderer-proxy`, which validates URL schemes, credentials, ports, every resolved IP, and pins the validated IP when opening the connection. Production only allows public unicast destinations on ports 80/443. Redirects and subresources pass through the same proxy. No browser TLS-verification bypass or stealth modifications are used. Chromium runs as the unprivileged `node` user with container capability drops, no-new-privileges, memory/process limits and fresh browser state; Chromium's own sandbox is disabled for container compatibility.

Do not expose the renderer or proxy ports. `deploy/compose.test.yaml` deliberately enables private destinations for the local fixture and must never be used for a production deployment.

## Extended audit coverage

- Hreflang: malformed codes/URLs, duplicate language entries, missing self-reference, non-indexable crawled targets and missing reciprocal links. In-scope alternates enter the crawl frontier. Out-of-scope or budget-excluded targets remain unknown.
- Soft 404: a short HTTP 200 page with a clear not-found title/H1 is flagged as a **heuristic**, not a confirmed missing page.
- URL hygiene: long URLs, uppercase/underscores in paths and excessive query parameters.
- Assets: up to 20 distinct same-origin image/script/stylesheet URLs per page, subject to robots, delay and SSRF policy. Reports HTTP 4xx/5xx and known sizes above 1 MiB. Blocks/rate limits stop that page's resource checks. Cross-origin and remaining resources are not checked; a missing size header is not an estimated size.

## Opt-in browser SERPs

Settings → Data providers → **Chromium (Bing, opt-in)** enables the adapter for the active workspace. It also requires the renderer service. This is direct Bing organic data, not Google data. It is the final fallback after Serper, Brave and SearXNG. It honors Bing robots.txt, uses an honest user agent, paces direct searches to one per ten seconds and stops on bot challenges; a challenge activates an hour cooldown in the service. Search markup changes, robots exclusions or provider blocks can make this adapter unavailable. During verification on 2026-11-11, Bing robots.txt disallowed search scraping, and the live adapter correctly refused the request; extraction was verified against a controlled browser fixture. No CAPTCHA or bot-check workaround is implemented. Provider-independent shared SERP caching remains seven days; explicit refresh requests fetch anew.

## Saved keyword refresh

**Refresh all** or **Refresh selected** creates a durable `saved_keyword_refresh` job. The selection is frozen at enqueue time, with one active refresh per project. The job checks project ownership, checkpoints every keyword and skips completed writes after a retry. Deleting a selected keyword while queued is safe. Tags and saved-keyword identity remain unchanged.

Refresh updates SERP difficulty, intent and features, plus Wikipedia-based volume/trend where the enabled demand provider has a matching article. The pageview cache retains its 30-day TTL. Missing estimates stay null; popularity remains the relative score of the originating research. Provider errors fail/retry the job and retain already completed progress. The saved-keywords screen shows the latest refresh state and error. Jobs use the existing workspace-scoped job API.

Endpoint: `POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/saved-keywords/refresh`, body `{ "ids": [] }` for all or a list of up to 1,000 IDs. Returns a job with HTTP 202. Poll `/api/v1/jobs/{job_id}` for status and `{done,total}` progress.

Google Trends remains deferred. PAA/related-search coverage remains provider-dependent. These limitations are not filled with invented metrics.

## Verification

`scripts/e2e-m2.py` uses the deterministic SERP response from the local badseo fixture. It checks bulk refresh selection, concurrency conflicts, project isolation, null metrics, preserved tags, rendered content and persisted Lighthouse scores. `scripts/e2e-audit.sh` covers the new rule types alongside M1 regressions. `cd renderer && npm test` covers public/private address checks, mixed DNS answers and both HTTP/CONNECT proxy denials.

The Integration checks GitHub workflow runs the isolated fixture stack on pull requests. Its optional `live_keywords` dispatch input also runs `scripts/e2e-keywords.sh` against live free suggestion/demand providers. To use live SearXNG with the test overlay, set `TEST_SEARXNG_URL=http://searxng:8080` and add `--profile serp`; the overlay otherwise uses the deterministic fixture.

title: Google Search Console
markdown:
# Google Search Console

M3 adds a project Search Console tab, a read-only Google OAuth connection, verified property selection, performance explorer, CSV export, URL inspection, and four MCP tools. Google credentials are optional; rank tracking and other features still work without them.

## Operator setup

1. In Google Cloud, enable **Google Search Console API**, configure the OAuth consent screen, and create a **Web application** OAuth client. When using a testing consent screen, add the Google accounts that will connect as test users.
2. Register this exact authorized redirect URI: `<WEB_BASE_URL>/api/v1/gsc/oauth/callback`. For the default local instance, use `http://localhost:3000/api/v1/gsc/oauth/callback`.
3. Set `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, and a stable `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in `.env`. The encryption key is base64 of 32 random bytes; keep a secure backup. Do not replace an existing key: it also encrypts provider credentials.
4. Recreate the application services with the usual Compose command. Open a project → **Search Console** → **Connect Google**, authorize read-only access, then choose **Use property**.

The user must complete real Google consent. The integration tests use a local fixture and do not prove that a particular Google Cloud client or live property is configured correctly.

## Behavior and limits

- Connections belong to a project, with one Google grant and selected property per project. Workspace admins can connect, select a verified property, or disconnect; members can read the selected property's data. An API key can use the GSC tools but cannot start or complete browser OAuth.
- OAuth requests only `webmasters.readonly`, asks for offline access, uses S256 PKCE, and stores a hashed, user/workspace/project-bound state with a 10-minute lifetime. State is consumed once, including declined or failed callbacks. Refresh tokens and PKCE verifiers are AES-GCM encrypted at rest. Access tokens are short-lived and kept only in memory for each operation. HTTP tracing excludes query strings.
- Each operation refreshes access from the stored grant. Revoked grants produce an instruction to reconnect; quota errors do not trigger automatic retries. Each request has a 15-second timeout and bounded response size.
- Disconnect deletes this project's local grant and pending OAuth state. It does not revoke the Google account's entire grant, which could disrupt other connected projects. Reconnecting resets the selected property so it must be selected again.
- Performance supports query/page/country/device/date/searchAppearance dimensions, AND filters, search types, and offset pagination. Dates must be within the last 16 months and exclude the latest three days. Requests return 1–1000 rows, default 100. Dates are interpreted by Google in Pacific Time. Google returns top rows and may omit anonymized queries; grouped rows must not be presented as whole-site totals.
- The UI exports the displayed page, with spreadsheet formula prefixes escaped. The API accepts the same query body at `POST /projects/{project_id}/gsc/performance.csv`; callers can paginate to export more pages.
- Inspection accepts 1–10 HTTP(S) URLs and returns Google's **indexed** version, not a live test or an indexing request. Invalid individual URLs return partial errors; connection/quota failures require correction before retrying. Google enforces whether a URL belongs to the selected domain or URL-prefix property. SeoSeo sends URLs to Google's fixed endpoint and does not fetch them directly.

## REST and MCP

All project routes are under `/api/v1/projects/{project_id}/gsc`:

| Method | Suffix | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET | (none) | Configuration/connection status without secrets |
| POST | `/connect` | Start browser OAuth |
| DELETE | (none) | Disconnect this project |
| GET | `/sites` | List verified properties |
| PUT | `/site` | Select an exact returned `site_url` |
| POST | `/performance` | Query measured traffic |
| POST | `/performance.csv` | Export one query page |
| POST | `/inspect` | Inspect 1–10 URLs |

Callback: `GET /api/v1/gsc/oauth/callback`, using the signed-in user who began the flow.

MCP: `list_search_console_sites`, `set_search_console_site`, `get_search_console_performance`, `inspect_urls`. All take an explicit `project_id` and use the same domain services as REST. Total server inventory: 33 tools.

## Offline verification

Use the existing throwaway `seoseo-ci` project and add `-f deploy/compose.gsc-test.yaml` to the test stack's Compose command. It supplies fake Google credentials, encryption key, endpoint overrides, and a local fixture on `127.0.0.1:3101`. Never use this overlay in production.

```sh
WEB_PORT=3100 WEB_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3100 docker compose -p seoseo-ci \
  -f deploy/compose.yaml -f deploy/compose.test.yaml -f deploy/compose.gsc-test.yaml \
  --env-file .env --profile renderer up -d --build
python scripts/e2e-gsc.py admin@example.com 'correct horse battery' http://127.0.0.1:3100
```

Run `scripts/smoke.sh` first if the test instance has no accounts. Run integration scripts sequentially because provider settings are shared within the test workspace. On Windows, `127.0.0.1` avoids the per-request delay observed with Python's `localhost` connections.

The endpoint overrides (`GOOGLE_AUTH_URL`, `GOOGLE_TOKEN_URL`, `GSC_API_URL`, `GSC_INSPECTION_URL`) are operator environment settings only, never client-supplied URLs. Production Compose keeps Google's defaults; test Compose overrides them explicitly.

References: [Google OAuth web-server flow](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/web-server), [Search Analytics query](https://developers.google.com/webmaster-tools/v1/searchanalytics/query), [property list](https://developers.google.com/webmaster-tools/v1/sites/list), [URL inspection](https://developers.google.com/webmaster-tools/v1/urlInspection.index/inspect).

title: 11 — Project memory and reports
markdown:
# 11 — Project memory and reports

M4's first delivery adds durable project context and self-contained HTML reports. Both are tenant-scoped in Postgres and available through REST, the web app, and MCP.

## Project memory

`GET/PUT /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/context` stores four typed collections:

- context sections (`key`, `title`, `content`, author source);
- competitors (`domain`, optional name and notes);
- key pages (`url`, role `hub|spoke|money|other`, optional topic);
- an immutable research log appended by the server.

The context is one bounded, revisioned document. A client must send the revision returned by its last read; a stale write returns `409 Conflict` instead of silently overwriting another person's or agent's changes. The initial revision is `0`. Limits are 20 sections, 50 competitors, 100 key pages, and the latest 100 research notes.

MCP tools: `get_project_context`, `update_project_context`.

## Reports

Reports contain a title, optional summary, complete HTML document, optional producing skill/template, and creator source. HTML is limited to 500 KiB. List responses omit HTML; the authenticated and public raw endpoints return it with a restrictive CSP (`sandbox`, no scripts, no forms, no external assets), `nosniff`, and no-referrer headers. The web viewer also uses a sandboxed iframe.

Templates are reusable instruction briefs, limited to 10 per project. REST supports create, list, update, and delete. MCP's `save_report_template` creates or updates when `template_id` is supplied.

Sharing generates a random 192-bit URL token. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored. The token is returned once and cannot be recovered; generating another token replaces it. Editing a report or explicitly revoking sharing immediately invalidates the old URL. Public metadata excludes the project id and report HTML; HTML is available only from the sandboxed raw endpoint.

MCP tools: `save_report`, `get_report`, `list_reports`, `delete_report`, `save_report_template`, `list_report_templates`, `delete_report_template`, `set_report_sharing`.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/cargo-docker.sh check --workspace`
- `bash scripts/cargo-docker.sh clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cd frontend && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm build`
- Apply migrations to a disposable database, run the API with `AUTH_MODE=none`, then run `python3 scripts/e2e-m4.py`.

title: 12 — Dashboard and website onboarding
markdown:
# 12 — Dashboard and website onboarding

M4 continuation adds DB-01/03/05 and the available portions of DB-02/WS-11. Migration `0008_dashboard.sql` is additive; never replace the applied `0007_memory_reports.sql` migration.

## Website setup

Creating a project with a website in the UI starts its first audit (50-page cap, robots.txt respected, rendering when configured), then opens `/p/{id}/onboarding`. API/MCP callers explicitly invoke website research. Concurrent requests lock the project and reuse the latest audit for the current domain, including completed/failed audits. Retry a failed audit from Site audit. A project remains saved if the initial request fails.

Setup shows up to five crawled pages and a draft formed from title, description and H1. This is source evidence, not LLM synthesis. The user reviews it, supplies their goal and explicitly saves. Manual entry works when a crawl fails. Saving replaces only `business_overview` and `current_goal`, adds selected evidence URLs, preserves other context/competitors/pages and appends a research note. Revision checks prevent lost updates; a project lock checks the expected domain and archive status at the write. Website text is untrusted input, never agent instructions.

## Dashboard

The overview shows six evidence-derived checklist steps, latest completed site health, running audit progress, saved-keyword/tracker/report counts and up to ten rank movers. Skip choices belong to the current user. Audit health matches the current website; changing domain hides the old site's audit. Rank movements compare adjacent completed measurements only when provider and depth match, excluding unknown positions and trackers for another domain/market.

Search keywords shows top queries, new queries and striking-distance query/page pairs with search, sorting, minimum impressions and 25-row pagination. All data is from Search Console web search; positions are averages, not live ranks. A visit requests a background refresh when data is missing/stale. Dates deliberately exclude four UTC days to avoid incomplete Pacific-time days.

- Top: 28 completed days, sorted by clicks.
- New: at least ten impressions in seven completed days with no returned observations in the preceding 28 days. If the baseline hits the 1,000-row cap, candidates are checked individually before being labeled new (maximum 25 candidates).
- Striking distance: query/page pairs with average position 5–20 inclusive, sorted by impressions.

Each period/view is capped at 1,000 rows. The UI discloses truncation and Google query omissions; these are sampled opportunities, not an exhaustive inventory.

## Refresh lifecycle and isolation

Refresh claims and jobs are created in one transaction under a project lock. Parallel visits reuse the same active job. Success is fresh for 24 hours; errors preserve the previous snapshot and back off 15 minutes. Queued workers resolve membership again. Snapshot identity includes project domain/market, selected property and connection timestamp. Reads and final writes compare identity, preventing old jobs from publishing data after project/property/grant changes. Disconnect immediately hides prior snapshots. No Google grant is required to use the rest of the dashboard.

REST and six MCP tools call the same domain services. Memory/report schemas and tools remain those shipped on the pulled branch; no duplicate document store is introduced. This delivery also fixes existing memory updates after revision 0 and rejects archived-project memory writes.

## Verification

Use a **disposable** Compose project with `compose.yaml`, `compose.test.yaml`, `compose.gsc-test.yaml` and `compose.dashboard-test.yaml`. The last overlay disables rendering to keep the offline onboarding test deterministic. Use password auth, open sign-up, a separate database/volumes, `WEB_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3200` and `WEB_PORT=3200`; the GSC fixture listens on loopback port 3101. Use separately tagged backend/web images so the normal stack is unaffected.

```powershell
python scripts/e2e-dashboard.py http://127.0.0.1:3200
$env:PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE = "$env:TEMP/seoseo-m4-browser/node_modules/playwright-core"
node scripts/e2e-m4-browser.cjs http://127.0.0.1:3200
```

The API regression covers concurrent audit/refresh claims, evidence review, repeated memory saves, preserved context, stale revisions/domain, cross-tenant access, GSC OAuth fixture, truncated baseline verification, source invalidation, provider quota backoff, MCP reads and archived-memory protection. Browser regression covers project creation through review/save, dashboard/navigation 390-pixel layouts and anonymous report sharing. Standard checks: Rust fmt, workspace tests, strict Clippy, frontend lint/typecheck/build, and Docker image/Compose startup.

## M4 completion

The remaining M4 implementation is now provided by [Integrations and OAuth](13-m4-integrations-and-oauth.md): optional model synthesis with explicit review, recorded link activity, GA4, IndexNow and MCP OAuth. Automatic backlink discovery remains M5.

Verified 2026-11-12: 58 Rust workspace tests, strict Clippy/fmt, frontend lint/typecheck and production builds, separate backend/web Docker images, fresh Compose migration/startup, dashboard API/MCP regression, existing Memory/Reports and GSC regressions, and Chrome desktop/mobile/anonymous-share checks.

title: M4 integrations, model drafts and MCP OAuth
markdown:
# M4 integrations, model drafts and MCP OAuth

This delivery completes the remaining M4 feature catalog work: GA4 IN-03, IndexNow IN-05, MCP OAuth MC-02, optional model synthesis for WS-11 and recorded link activity for DB-02. Migrations `0009_m4_integrations.sql` and `0010_mcp_oauth.sql` are additive. Existing migrations and project memory/report contracts stay intact.

## Google Analytics 4

Open a project's **Integrations** tab. Configure `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` and the existing stable `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. Enable the Google Analytics Admin and Data APIs in the operator's Google Cloud project. Register `{WEB_BASE_URL}/api/v1/ga4/oauth/callback` on the OAuth client, in addition to the existing Search Console callback.

Analytics uses its own read-only `analytics.readonly` grant, encrypted per project. It does not add scopes to Search Console, and disconnecting either integration does not disconnect the other. Browser-session admins connect and choose properties; current project members can read reports. Consent state is short-lived, single-use and bound to the initiating user/workspace/project. Refresh-token rotation updates only the grant originally read, preserving reconnects and existing tokens when Google omits a replacement.

Property discovery paginates `accountSummaries.list`. Selection verifies the exact numeric `properties/{id}` against fresh discovery (up to 20 pages). Reports cannot supply arbitrary properties, dimensions, metrics or provider URLs.

Nine fixed REST/MCP reports are available: organic overview, organic landing pages, page performance, traffic acquisition, key events, ecommerce performance, site search, audience breakdown and measurement health. Organic overview/landing pages/page performance/key events/ecommerce filter to the session Organic Search channel. Acquisition, audience and measurement health cover all channels; site search filters the `view_search_results` event. Every response identifies the channel.

Reports require explicit ordered dates, at most 366 days, ending at least two UTC days ago, and at most 1,000 rows per page (UI pages are 100 rows). This conservative lag excludes incomplete property days. Google metadata retains the property's reporting time zone/currency, privacy thresholding, row count and quota. Restricted metric values become null. Omitted/thresholded rows are not synthesized as zero. GA4 counts are not interchangeable with Search Console attribution. Measurement health summarizes received events; it does not prove a tag is correctly installed.

## IndexNow

An admin creates/reuses one public ownership key per current project domain and downloads `{key}.txt` from Integrations. Place that file at the root of each submitted host. A domain change rotates the local key; it cannot silently reuse a previously configured site's key.

Verification uses the crawler's guarded DNS resolver, a 1 KB body limit and no redirects. The response must be HTTP 200 with exactly the key (surrounding whitespace allowed). Missing, redirected or inconclusive ownership stops submission for that host. Production checks use HTTPS; the private-crawler test mode permits HTTP fixtures. Engine endpoints are operator configuration only (`INDEXNOW_URL`, default the protocol endpoint), never project input.

Submit 1–1,000 changed URLs across at most ten project-domain/subdomain hosts. Credentials and non-default ports are rejected. URLs are deduplicated, grouped by host and sent with the matching root keyLocation. A database claim enforces a one-minute project cooldown and rejects concurrent or stale-domain submissions. Host requests run with bounded concurrency/timeouts. HTTP 200 means received; 202 means engine ownership validation is pending. Neither guarantees indexing. No automatic resubmission of audit pages is enabled: automatic change detection belongs to later audit comparison work.

## Optional website synthesis

Set `OPENAI_COMPAT_BASE_URL` and `LLM_MODEL`; optionally set `OPENAI_COMPAT_API_KEY`. For local Ollama in Docker, an example base is `http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1` with an installed compatible model. Operator-controlled endpoints may be internal; projects cannot set them. With no endpoint, manual onboarding remains fully usable.

**Generate model draft** sends up to five bounded crawl-evidence records to a chat-completions-compatible model. No call happens until explicitly requested. Website content is labeled untrusted data, and the model receives no tools. JSON output is size/field validated. The draft shows an overview, suggested goal and caveat. Applying it edits the form only; memory changes require the existing explicit review/save action with revision and expected-domain checks. Model errors and invalid JSON never write memory.

## Recorded link activity

Users/agents can record source/target pairs with an observed live/lost state. Targets must belong to the project's domain. Only admins write; members read. The project caps observations at 10,000 and reads return the latest 100; the dashboard displays the latest five. Repeating an identical state preserves the original observation time. Updating live/lost changes the recorded state/time. Current-domain reads hide old website observations, and writes compare the expected domain under the project lock. This is user-provided evidence, clearly labeled in the UI; it does not claim an exhaustive backlink index or independently verified source status. Automatic backlink discovery and new/lost/live backlink analysis remain M5 scope.

## MCP OAuth

Existing `seo_` API keys continue to work. OAuth protects only the canonical `{WEB_BASE_URL}/mcp` resource; OAuth access tokens cannot authenticate REST endpoints. Browser OAuth/MCP clients can use CORS in password mode, but cross-origin MCP calls must present a bearer; cookie-only requests from another origin are refused. Authenticated REST routes keep the app-origin-only CORS policy. No-auth mode does not enable cross-origin MCP. Use HTTPS and secure cookies for a public deployment. OAuth consent requires password-authenticated browser sessions; trusted-network no-auth mode does not issue OAuth grants.

Discovery endpoints:

- `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`
- `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`

Public-client DCR is `POST /oauth/register` with exact HTTPS or loopback redirect URIs, `token_endpoint_auth_method: none`, and authorization-code/refresh-token grants. Registration is capped at 100/hour and 10,000 clients per instance, under a database lock. No remote client metadata or logo URL is fetched. Client-ID metadata documents and confidential clients are not supported in this initial DCR implementation.

`GET /oauth/authorize` validates the client, exact registered redirect, canonical resource, `scope=mcp`, `response_type=code` and S256 PKCE challenge before showing consent. Invalid redirects are never used for error redirects. The consent screen names the app, return address, resource and currently selected workspace. Approval permits MCP actions with the user's current role in that workspace. Denial returns `access_denied` and the original state. The authenticated consent POST requires CSRF protection and cannot use API-key/OAuth credentials.

`POST /oauth/token` exchanges a five-minute single-use code and valid verifier, or rotates a refresh token. Access tokens expire in one hour, refresh tokens in 30 days, and grants have a 90-day maximum lifetime. Bearer/code/refresh secrets are stored only as hashes. Tokens are resource- and client-bound. Code replay revokes the issued grant; refresh-token replay revokes the whole family. Clients must serialize refresh requests. Membership/role are resolved on every MCP call, so removal immediately stops access and downgrades do not retain old privileges.

Revoke through `POST /oauth/revoke` or **Connected apps** in Settings. A user sees/revokes only their own grants in the current workspace. Token and registration responses use no-store headers; traces use route templates, not OAuth query strings or bearer secrets. Storage contains a bounded number of pending consent codes per user. Operators should additionally apply their normal ingress rate limits to public endpoints.

## API and MCP

REST includes `/projects/{id}/ga4`, `/ga4/connect`, `/ga4/properties`, `/ga4/property`, `/ga4/reports/{kind}`, `/indexnow/{setup,verify,submit}`, `/links` and `/website-synthesis`. Google callback is `/api/v1/ga4/oauth/callback`. Workspace consent/grant endpoints are under `/api/v1/oauth/`; standard public OAuth endpoints are outside the API prefix. Generated OpenAPI covers authenticated feature routes; public OAuth metadata describes standard protocol routes.

17 added MCP tools (66 total): property list/selection, nine fixed Analytics reports, IndexNow setup/verification/submission, website synthesis, and link observation list/save. They call the same domain services as REST.

## Verification

Use a disposable Compose project with the base, test, GSC-test, dashboard-test and `compose.m4-final-test.yaml` overlays. Password auth/open signup, separate database/volumes and separately tagged images are required. The final overlay uses local fixtures for Analytics, IndexNow and a model; no real Google, indexing or paid model actions are performed. Set `WEB_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3300` and `WEB_PORT=3300`; the existing fixture origin is loopback port 3101.

```powershell
python scripts/e2e-m4-final.py http://127.0.0.1:3300
$env:PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE = "$env:TEMP/seoseo-m4-browser/node_modules/playwright-core"
node scripts/e2e-m4-final-browser.cjs http://127.0.0.1:3300
```

Keep existing dashboard, GSC and Memory/Reports regressions green. Live Google credentials/consent, real engine acceptance and a real local model remain operator verification. Fixture success does not prove access to a production account.

Protocol references: [GA4 report basics](https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/reporting/data/v1/basics), [GA4 schema](https://developers.google.com/analytics/devguides/reporting/data/v1/api-schema), [IndexNow protocol](https://www.indexnow.org/documentation), [MCP authorization](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/authorization).

Validation on 2026-11-12: 61 Rust workspace tests, strict Clippy/fmt, frontend lint/typecheck/production build, separate Docker images and fresh Compose migrations. API/MCP fixtures cover nine GA4 reports, model failure/no implicit saves, IndexNow ownership/cooldown, live member-role enforcement, OAuth PKCE/resource/CSRF/rotation/replay/revocation and CORS boundaries. Chrome covers model review/save, GA4 connect/nine reports, IndexNow, recorded links, consent/exchange/revoke and mobile layouts. Existing dashboard, GSC and Memory/Reports regressions remain green.

title: Competitive domain research
markdown:
# Competitive domain research

The project's **Competitive** tab and `get_domain_overview` MCP tool inspect a domain against locally available search evidence. DO-01 through DO-05 use an explicitly bounded evidence sample. On-demand domain age (DO-07) is available separately. See the M5 acceptance record for verification limits.

## Evidence and limits

- Scope is the union of saved keywords, research ideas, rank-tracker keywords and imported competitive-volume keywords belonging to the authorized project, filtered to one country/language. The project market is the default. Other projects' keyword lists never enter the scope.
- Sample the first 500 distinct keywords alphabetically. `scope_keywords` reports the full scope and `sampled_keywords` the bounded sample.
- Use the newest cached snapshot per keyword from the last 30 days, including empty results. Newer metasearch snapshots replace older exact snapshots. Each keyword includes provider, exact flag and timestamp.
- Only positions 1–30 count. Group by registrable domain using existing public-suffix rules; choose the best position once per domain/keyword. Subdomains roll up to the same domain.
- `checked_keywords` includes recent empty snapshots; missing/expired snapshots are unchecked. Coverage includes keywords where the requested domain was absent.
- Return observed keyword count, position distribution, best-result URLs, domains sharing observed keywords, and keyword gaps against the project's website. Gaps mean absence from the sampled page; they do not prove a domain does not rank.
- Keywords are paginated (default 100, maximum 500; `limit`/`offset`), pages and gaps are capped at 100 each; competitors at 50. Totals/distribution use the full bounded sample. Pages count only each keyword's best result URL.
- SeoSeo Rank uses the separately imported Common Crawl graph and its source/release metadata. Monthly sample clicks use eligible imported search counts, as described below. The domain sample has source `project_serp_sample` and confidence `relative`; it is not a comprehensive domain index.

SERP inspection is read-only and makes no external requests. Build coverage with keyword research or saved-keyword refresh, then reload evidence. Optional volume imports use additive migration 0014; inspecting stored evidence requires no credentials.

## Domain registration age (DO-07)

Click **Check registration age** after inspecting a domain to request public registry metadata. This action is separate from SERP inspection; it also works when the project has no keyword evidence. `POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/domain-age` accepts `{ "domain": "example.com" }`, or `{}` to use the project website. MCP `get_domain_age` takes `project_id` and optional `domain`.

Discovery uses the fixed [IANA DNS bootstrap](https://data.iana.org/rdap/dns.json), matching the longest domain-label suffix per [RFC 9224](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9224.html). Only public HTTPS registry endpoints on port 443 are supported, with guarded DNS, no proxies, no redirects/referrals, a 1 MiB response limit, 15-second request timeouts and one-second pacing. The domain's own website is never fetched. HTTP-only registries and registries requiring redirects are reported as unsupported or unavailable; 403/429 stop the lookup.

Only a matching domain object and its top-level `registration` events from [RFC 9083](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9083.html) are used. Last-changed, transfer and expiration dates never substitute for registration. Invalid/future registration dates are ignored; if multiple valid events exist, the earliest is used. This is the registry's reported registration date, not proof of website age or continuous ownership. No record (404), missing date and unsupported service leave `age_days` null; a 404 does not establish domain availability.

The existing shared provider cache stores the IANA bootstrap and minimal parsed registration records for 24 hours, including negative/unsupported results. No raw RDAP response, entity/contact data or registrar details are stored. Age is recalculated in whole days at read time; no forced-refresh bypass is exposed. Network, malformed-response and block errors are surfaced without caching a false unknown record. Every read authorizes the project before using the shared cache or network. No new schema or operator credentials are needed.

## API and MCP

`GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/domain-overview?domain=example.com&country=US&language=en&limit=100&offset=0`

All query parameters are optional; domain defaults to the project website. A project without a website must supply `domain`. Domains and HTTP(S) website URLs normalize to registrable domains. Members can read, including archived projects; cross-organization access returns 404.

MCP `get_domain_overview` takes `project_id` and the same optional query fields, returning the same result in the standard envelope.

## Verification

`cargo test -j 1 --workspace` covers aggregation, deduplication, gaps, unknown metrics, normalization, RDAP discovery/date parsing, response limits and HTTP block/redirect handling. `python scripts/e2e-competitive.py http://127.0.0.1:3401 seoseo-m5-db` targets a disposable API/database with password auth and open signup. It seeds synthetic SERPs and cache metadata through the named database container and verifies latest/empty/expired snapshots, research-only scope, market/project/tenant isolation, validation, the 500-keyword bound, domain-age caching/expiry/unknown handling and REST/MCP parity. Never run this fixture script against production.

## Monthly sample click estimates

Admins of active projects can import up to 1,000 keyword/monthly-search-count rows per request, scoped to country/language, with a source/period label (maximum 100 characters). `POST /projects/{project_id}/competitive-volumes` and MCP `import_competitive_search_volumes` accept `{country,language,source_label,rows:[{keyword,monthly_search_volume}]}`. Upserts serialize under the project lock; at most 10,000 stored market/keyword rows per project. The UI accepts the same JSON.

Counts expire from estimates after 90 days. Only the newest **exact** SERP snapshot qualifies. Per-keyword estimated clicks = monthly search count × `0.28 / position^1.5`; this is an explicit heuristic, not a fitted CTR model. `estimated_monthly_traffic` is a rounded **observed sample** estimate, populated only when every matched keyword has eligible volume. With partial coverage it stays null; `partial_sample_estimated_clicks` and coverage report the known subtotal. Neither field establishes total domain traffic. No matches or no eligible counts remains unknown. Source labels travel with each keyword. Wikipedia pageviews are never used as monthly search counts.

title: Backlink discovery and snapshot evidence
markdown:
# Backlink discovery and snapshot evidence

The **Backlinks** project tab supports guarded source-page discovery, rechecks, imported samples, comparable snapshot history, groups, explainable HTML risk scores and new/lost pairs through REST/UI/MCP. Existing M4 individual link observations stay separate. Coverage is a bounded sample, never a comprehensive backlink index.

## Import and comparison rules

An admin of an active project imports a complete JSON array with at most 1,000 distinct source/target URL pairs, within the API's 2 MiB request limit. The UI accepts a file or pasted JSON. Example row:

```json
{
  "source_url": "https://publisher.example/article",
  "target_url": "https://your-project.example/page",
  "anchor": "Optional anchor text",
  "nofollow": null
}
```

Each import supplies a stable lowercase `dataset` key, the exact current project website in `expected_domain`, and `complete_sample: true`. The confirmation means these rows replace this dataset's entire sample, including an empty array. Do not use the same dataset key for partial/differently scoped exports.

Only public HTTP(S) URLs with default ports and no credentials are accepted; URL fragments are removed. Target hosts must equal the project website or one of its subdomains with a label-boundary match. Sources must have a different registrable domain. URLs are capped at 2,048 bytes each, anchors at 500 characters, and normalized duplicate source/target pairs are rejected. Links are counted as URL pairs, not individual hyperlink occurrences. Anchor and nofollow values remain null when unspecified; an empty anchor is distinct from unknown.

The first import for a website/dataset is a baseline: all pairs have state `live`, with no new/lost claims. Later imports compare against the most recent remaining snapshot for that exact website/dataset/source:

- `live`: pair remains in the sample; current metadata replaces previous metadata.
- `new`: pair is present now but was absent from the previous sample.
- `lost`: pair was in the previous sample but is absent now. Its metadata comes from that previous sample.

`live_count` includes both `live` and `new`. These states describe **sample membership**; a lost pair does not establish that a link was removed from the web. A recurring pair becomes new if it was absent from the immediately previous sample. Old lost rows do not accumulate across snapshots.

Imports, quota checks, baseline selection and deletions serialize under the project-row lock. Snapshot timestamps use the actual insertion clock after acquiring that lock, so concurrent imports form an ordered chain. A snapshot and all its rows commit atomically. Reads use a repeatable-read transaction for consistent metadata/rows during deletion or website changes. Migration `0011_backlink_snapshots.sql` is additive.

## Reading and retention

Members can read. Details are available only for the current project website, including while archived. History metadata lists up to 100 snapshots across all website identities so admins can delete old samples and recover quota. Changing the project website starts an independent comparison history and hides old evidence details. Stale imports are rejected under the write lock.

The table supports `all`, `live` (includes new), `new`, and `lost` filters with up to 200 rows per page (default 100). A snapshot has at most 1,000 current pairs plus 1,000 lost pairs. Referring domains, top target pages and anchor groups aggregate only current membership, independently of pagination/filtering, with the top 100 groups returned for each. Imported spam scores remain null. Views label the source `user_import` or `serp_crawl`, with confidence `relative`.

At most 100 snapshots per project are retained, including previous websites. An admin can delete a snapshot in an active project. Other snapshots retain their recorded counts and comparison ID/timestamp even if the comparison snapshot is deleted. Future imports compare against the latest remaining snapshot in that dataset/website. Deleting the latest snapshot therefore changes the next import's baseline. Project deletion cascades to snapshots and evidence.

## REST and MCP

- `GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/backlink-snapshots` / `list_backlink_snapshots`: history metadata.
- `POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/backlink-snapshots` / `import_backlink_snapshot`: import `{expected_domain,dataset,complete_sample,links}`.
- `GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/backlink-snapshots/{snapshot_id}?state=all&limit=100&offset=0` / `get_backlink_snapshot`: evidence, summary and groups.
- `DELETE /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/backlink-snapshots/{snapshot_id}` / `delete_backlink_snapshot`: delete one sample.

MCP takes explicit `project_id`/`snapshot_id` fields and uses the same domain services as REST. Only admins can import/delete; cross-project/organization IDs cannot access evidence. Imports require no external provider. Discovery may use configured free SearXNG or optional BYOK search.

## Verification

`python scripts/e2e-backlinks.py http://127.0.0.1:3401 seoseo-m5links-db` targets a disposable password-auth stack with open signup and a named test DB container. It verifies baseline/change/empty/reappearance semantics, aggregates, validation, member/tenant/project isolation, stable historical diffs, concurrent baseline/100-snapshot quota enforcement, website changes, archived reads and MCP parity. It writes fixture members/snapshots directly through `docker exec psql`; never point it at production.

`scripts/e2e-backlinks-browser.cjs` tests baseline/change imports and lost-state filtering in a temporary headless Chrome profile, captures desktop/mobile screenshots and checks for browser errors and page overflow. Install `puppeteer-core` outside the repository and set `PUPPETEER_MODULE` to its module path; set `CHROME_PATH` if needed. Run `node scripts/e2e-backlinks-browser.cjs http://127.0.0.1:3400 OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` against the disposable stack only.

## Discovery and verified rechecks

`POST /projects/{project_id}/backlink-discoveries` / MCP `discover_backlinks` accepts `{expected_domain,search,source_urls}`. Search is an explicit opt-in; up to 20 additional public external source URLs may be supplied. Without search, rechecks work from the previous crawl sample or explicit sources. `GET` / `list_backlink_discoveries` returns the last 20 job statuses, polled by the UI. Only admins of active projects start work; readers remain tenant/current-website scoped. There is one active discovery per project, a one-minute cooldown and a 100-snapshot project quota.

Search discovers candidates with a domain-reference query, then verifies actual HTML hyperlinks. Prior crawl source pages are checked first. At most 40 pages, 1 MiB each, 10-second requests; robots status 200/404/410 required, exclusions and crawl delays respected (minimum one second; delays above 30 seconds skipped). DNS/SSRF protection, no proxies or redirects, default ports, public source/target URLs, website identity checks and stop-on-401/403/429 apply. HTML challenges, meta refresh, tiny SPA shells, extraction limits, unsupported responses and network failures are inconclusive. This is **SERP/explicit-source discovery**, not a Common Crawl inbound index: a CC URL-prefix index finds source URLs, not all pages linking to a target.

Each pair records `verification`, last `verified_at`, relation and risk evidence. `verified` means read on a successful source page; `unconfirmed` preserves a prior pair whose source could not be conclusively checked; `missing` means absent on successfully read HTML or a definitive 404/410 source. A SERP omission alone never establishes loss. Unknown rows retain their prior observation date but have no current risk score. Imported and crawl histories are separate even with the same dataset name. A job's completed status and its full snapshot commit atomically. A sample exceeding 1,000 current pairs fails while preserving the previous snapshot.

Risk is a transparent 0–100 heuristic for verified current pairs: 40 for a source below 100 words, 40 for over 80% external links when there are at least 20 links, 20 for anchor text over 120 characters. Saved reason codes explain each contribution. The summary averages scored current pairs and reports their coverage. A zero is a computed result; null means unscored. This is not malware detection, link quality authority or a search penalty verdict.

`GET /projects/{project_id}/dashboard/backlinks` / `get_dashboard_backlinks` returns the current website's latest full summary plus history. Migration 0014 is additive. The UI exposes discovery polling, provenance/coverage, verification dates, risk reasons, sample filters and grouping alongside manual imports. End-to-end verification is documented in [M5 acceptance](17-m5-acceptance.md).

title: AI visibility: engines, schedules and answer evidence
markdown:
# AI visibility: engines, schedules and answer evidence

Immutable trackers, durable manual or scheduled runs, question drafts, native engines, structured citations, literal mention rates, share of tracked mentions, retained-run trends and JSON export are available in the web app, REST and MCP. Results describe an API prompt sample, not consumer chat visibility or independently verified recommendations.

## Operator setup

The API and worker must use the same operator-controlled compatible gateway and approved model list:

```dotenv
OPENAI_COMPAT_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1
OPENAI_COMPAT_API_KEY=
AI_VISIBILITY_MODELS=installed-model-a,installed-model-b,installed-model-c
```

Use actual model identifiers installed/available at your gateway. [Ollama's compatible API](https://docs.ollama.com/api/openai-compatibility) supports the chat-completions interface used here. `AI_VISIBILITY_MODELS` allows up to 10 unique comma-separated model identifiers; if empty, it falls back to the existing `LLM_MODEL`. Each tracker chooses at most three. Native Ollama, Anthropic and Gemini can also be configured alongside the compatible gateway; at most 20 approved IDs across all adapters. Selecting three models does not establish three consumer chat engines. A paid gateway may bill the operator's account; local Ollama requires no paid key. Actual installed models and live gateway access remain operator setup, separate from offline fixture validation.

Project inputs cannot set the endpoint, credentials or arbitrary model IDs. Only the operator environment controls the gateway. The endpoint must be an HTTP(S) base URL without embedded credentials, query or fragment. Redirects and environment proxies are disabled; private/local endpoints are allowed because the URL is operator configuration. The model-list endpoint returns readiness and IDs, never the key or URL. Changes to the gateway after queuing fail that run before any call; a removed model also stops collection.

## Trackers and explicit runs

Admins of active projects create trackers with an exact `expected_domain`, name, 1–10 brand terms (80 characters each), 1–10 prompts (500 characters each), 1–3 approved models and country/language (default project market). Terms/prompts are trimmed and case-insensitive duplicates rejected. Tracker creation makes no model request. Configurations are immutable; create another tracker to change prompts/models/terms. The UI accepts one term/prompt per line; REST supports multiline prompt strings.

**Run model comparison** explicitly queues up to 30 requests. It freezes all tracker inputs, the requested market and a gateway fingerprint in the same transaction as the job. The system instruction supplies the requested country/language but no tracked terms; terms are used only when scoring the answer. This avoids automatically inserting the expected brand into otherwise unbranded prompts. Prompts supplied by the user can still bias the sample. Country/language are requested model context, not geographic measurement. Compatible/local engines receive no web tools. Native Anthropic requests provider-side web search; the model decides whether to use it. Gemini uses standard text generation without Google Search.

Compatible/local requests are sequential, paced at least one second apart per worker process, with temperature 0, a 1,500-token output request, 45-second timeout, 128 KiB response cap and 20,000-character text cap. A normal nonempty text answer with `finish_reason=stop` is required; truncated/empty/filtered/tool-call responses are failures. Model aliases/weights can change at the gateway; frozen inputs do not guarantee repeatability.

The job checkpoints each model/prompt cell to Postgres. A resumed worker skips persisted successes. Provider/network/format failures save an error cell, fail the run and stop further calls; collected answers remain available. Internal database/queue failures may retry through the existing durable queue. Terminal queue failures are reconciled to failed runs when read or before another run. A crash between an external request and storing its result may repeat that request on resume; this is not an exactly-once external API guarantee.

There is one active run per tracker, at most two per project, and a one-minute cooldown between retained runs for a tracker. Limits are serialized under the project lock. There are at most 10 trackers per project and 20 retained runs per tracker. Admins can delete completed trackers/runs for quota cleanup; active runs prevent deletion for that tracker. Archived projects remain readable. A website change hides previous-website details and stops subsequent worker requests for those trackers; prior tracker metadata remains available for cleanup. A request already in flight may finish, but its answer is not intentionally committed after the worker detects a changed/archived project.

## Meaning of the results

- Every view includes expected, successful and failed answer counts. Cells without a saved answer may be pending, interrupted or unattempted; they are distinct from measured absence.
- Terms match case-insensitively with Unicode alphanumeric boundaries across the full answer text. This is literal occurrence, not sentiment, endorsement, rank or recommendation. Configure explicit aliases as separate tracked terms when useful.
- Each term's `mention_rate_pct` is its number of matching successful answers divided by all successful answers. With no successful answers it is null, not zero. Failed/uncollected cells never enter the denominator. Several terms can match one answer, so rates need not sum to 100%; the separate `share_of_voice_pct` divides that term's matching-answer count by the sum of all tracked term/answer matches. It is null when none matched. This is share within the configured term sample, not a market-wide share.
- Up to 20 unique public HTTP(S) URLs are extracted from answer text. They are model-reported, unverified strings, not validated citations or evidence that the model browsed a page. Credentials/private-address URLs are excluded, no URL is fetched, and the answer viewer renders plain escaped text.
- Source is `model_api`, confidence `relative`. Run JSON export includes frozen configuration, raw text answers, matches, URLs, errors and coverage. It contains user prompt/answer data and is tenant-scoped, with no public share route.

## API and MCP

- `GET /api/v1/ai-visibility/models` / `list_ai_visibility_models`
- `GET|POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/ai-trackers` / `list_ai_visibility_trackers`, `create_ai_visibility_tracker`
- `GET|DELETE /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/ai-trackers/{tracker_id}` / `get_ai_visibility_tracker`, `delete_ai_visibility_tracker`
- `POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/ai-trackers/{tracker_id}/runs` / `run_ai_visibility_tracker`, body `{ "expected_domain": "example.com" }`
- `GET|DELETE /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/ai-trackers/{tracker_id}/runs/{run_id}` / `get_ai_visibility_run`, `delete_ai_visibility_run`

Members read; admins create/run/delete. MCP invokes the same domain services as REST. Additive migration `0012_ai_visibility.sql` adds trackers, runs and answer cells. No applied migration is changed.

## Verification

`scripts/ai-model-fixture.py` is a local compatible gateway for offline tests, not a model implementation. Configure API/worker with its `/v1` URL and models `fixture-a,fixture-b,fixture-c` on a disposable password-auth stack with open signup. `python scripts/e2e-ai-visibility.py http://127.0.0.1:3401 seoseo-m5ai-db seoseo-m5ai-worker http://127.0.0.1:3402` verifies three-model collection, frozen prompts, mention rates/unknowns, partial failures/truncation, checkpoint resume, queue reconciliation, changed gateway identity, concurrency/retention limits, role/tenant/project/website isolation, deletion and MCP parity. It pauses the named test worker and seeds fixtures through `docker exec psql`; never run against production.

`node scripts/e2e-ai-browser.cjs http://127.0.0.1:3400 OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` uses the same disposable fixture stack and a temporary `puppeteer-core` installation via `PUPPETEER_MODULE`. It checks tracker creation, explicit queueing/polling, rates, expanded answers and desktop/mobile layouts; `CHROME_PATH` overrides the browser executable. These legacy fixtures do not establish live provider access. The final M5 regression separately exercises real local Ollama; cloud engine live checks require credentials.

## Native engines and UTC schedules

Configure API and worker identically. These are operator settings, not project endpoint inputs:

```dotenv
AI_OLLAMA_URL=http://ollama:11434/v1
AI_OLLAMA_MODELS=your-installed-model
AI_ANTHROPIC_MODEL=your-search-capable-claude-model
AI_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
AI_GEMINI_MODEL=your-search-capable-gemini-model
AI_GEMINI_API_KEY=
```

The model list prefixes native IDs with `ollama/`, `anthropic/`, `gemini/`. Enable the Compose `ollama` profile and install a model using `docker compose ... exec ollama ollama pull <model>`; downloading/serving a model requires memory/disk appropriate to its size. Cloud keys/models are optional; the free local default works without them. Compatible gateway fallback to `LLM_MODEL` remains supported.

Anthropic uses Messages with `web_search_20250305` (maximum two searches per answer), requires normal `end_turn` completion and fails on search-tool errors. Gemini uses standard `generateContent` without tools, requires STOP and excludes thought parts. Unexpected grounding metadata is rejected rather than collected. Native requests have a 60-second timeout, 256 KiB body cap and 20,000-character answer cap. Redirects/proxies are disabled. 401/403/429 stop collection with a saved error. Endpoint overrides `AI_ANTHROPIC_URL` / `AI_GEMINI_URL` exist only for operators and disposable fixtures.

`engine` and `grounding` accompany every answer: `none` for Gemini/compatible/local, `provider_citations` for structured Anthropic citations, `requested_no_citations` when Anthropic search was requested but none returned. Up to 20 distinct public provider citation URLs/titles are retained, distinct from URLs found in model text. No citation target is fetched. The answer viewer displays provider citation links and escaped text. Provider citations still do not guarantee that every claim is correct. See the [Anthropic web search contract](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool).

Google Search grounding is deliberately not requested for durable Gemini trackers: its [use restrictions](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms#grounding-with-google-search) restrict automated collection and analysis of grounded results. Standard Gemini model comparisons still work, clearly labelled without grounding. Google AI Overview capture remains separate M6 scope.

`PATCH /projects/{project_id}/ai-trackers/{tracker_id}/schedule` / MCP `set_ai_visibility_schedule` accepts `{schedule,hour_utc,weekday}`: manual/daily/weekly/monthly, hour 0–23, ISO weekday 1–7. Monthly means day 1. Manual is the default. Saving a periodic schedule explicitly authorizes future collection with the tracker's request budget. The worker checks due schedules every 60 seconds; due claims and advancing next-run time serialize under the project lock. Multiple workers cannot claim the same occurrence. Busy/cooldown cycles are skipped. No catch-up burst. Removed models or the 20-run retention limit pause collection with an error and preserve evidence; clean up and save a schedule to resume. Archived projects and trackers for a different current website are excluded from due selection; restoring the same active website can make their saved schedule due again. Disabling uses manual.

`POST /projects/{project_id}/ai-prompt-research` / MCP `research_ai_visibility_prompts` makes one explicit approved-model request for 1–10 draft questions. It saves nothing. The UI requires reviewing/applying the draft before tracker creation. These are model suggestions, not measured prompt demand. `GET /.../ai-trackers/{tracker_id}/summary` / `get_ai_visibility_summary` returns retained-run coverage/rates and provider-citation domain counts (distinct answer cells per domain), keeping gateway fingerprints so changed engines are visible. No trends are synthesized between missing runs. Migration 0013 adds schedules and provenance without changing applied migrations.

title: M5 implementation and acceptance
markdown:
# M5 implementation and acceptance

M5 implementation covers DO-01..05/07, BL-01..06, DB-04, AI-01..04 and MC-05. The exact roadmap acceptance gate requiring **three live AI engines including Ollama remains pending**. Local Ollama was run successfully; Anthropic and Gemini have offline contract checks, not verified live accounts. No cloud credentials were available in this workspace.

## Delivered behavior

| Area | Implementation | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Competitive | Overview/SR, observed keywords and distribution, pages, competitors, gaps, RDAP age, volume import and sample-click estimates | Up to 500 project keywords; exact ranks and eligible monthly search counts required for estimates; never total domain traffic |
| Backlinks | Search/explicit-source discovery, robots-aware HTML verification, rechecks, imported samples, history, groups, filters, risk reasons and dashboard API | Up to 40 source pages/1,000 current pairs; failures retain prior evidence as unconfirmed; no exhaustive inbound index |
| AI | Compatible gateway plus native Ollama, Anthropic and Gemini; schedules, question drafts, durable answers, literal rates, share of tracked mentions, trends, citations and JSON export | Anthropic requests web search; Gemini/local/compatible have no web tools. Country/language are requested context, not measured location |
| Agents | Fourteen portable SeoSeo skills, display metadata, install/connection guide, upstream attribution and validator | Self-hosted MCP server only; no global installation or invented M6 capabilities |

There are 87 MCP tools. New schema is additive: 0013 schedules/citation provenance, 0014 search volumes/discovery/verification. Existing migrations remain unchanged. Normal deployments must rebuild the API/worker/web images and run migrations. Existing local deployment data was not migrated during acceptance work.

## Verified

- Rust formatting, strict workspace Clippy and all 76 workspace unit tests.
- Generated OpenAPI/TypeScript, frontend typecheck/lint and production Docker builds.
- Isolated Compose startup with Postgres, Valkey, migrations, API, web and workers. Two workers exercise the same due schedule without duplicate runs; retention pauses at 20 runs and preserves evidence.
- Existing competitive, imported-backlink and AI regressions: roles, tenant/project/current-website isolation, validation, concurrent quotas, durable partial failures/resume and REST/MCP parity.
- Final M5 regression: real local Ollama `smollm2:135m`; native Anthropic request/auth/search/citation fixture; native Gemini text-only request/auth fixture; drafts, rates/trends, schedules, eligible/partial click estimates, robots, blocked/redirect unknowns, verified missing links, over-limit snapshot preservation and dashboard/MCP parity.
- Headless Chrome desktop (1440px) and mobile (390px): draft review/apply, tracker collection, citation links/trends, schedule save/disable, discovery polling/risk and volume import/estimates. No page errors or document overflow. Screenshots were visually inspected.
- All fourteen skills pass the skill-creator validator and the repository tool-reference validator.

Fixture output is synthetic and explicitly labelled. The tiny local model proves API integration, not answer quality. Fixture checks do not establish real cloud credentials, billing, model availability or search permissions. Live free SERP coverage depends on the configured provider; the crawl regression uses local HTML fixtures.

Follow-up connection check: the installed, unmodified Claude Code CLI 2.1.304 is authenticated through Claude.ai and returned a successful live `claude-haiku-5-5` answer in print/JSON mode. Tools, MCP servers, customizations and session persistence were disabled for that check; no login tokens were extracted or copied. This confirms the local Claude Code connection only. It does not exercise SeoSeo's Anthropic HTTP adapter, provide Gemini access, or satisfy the three-engine saved-run gate. No direct cloud API credentials were found in the project environment, API/worker configuration or process/user/machine environment. See [Anthropic's authentication guidance](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance#authentication-and-credential-use) for the distinction between subscription login and application API authentication.

## Reproduce on a disposable stack

Run from the repository root. The test overlay disables private-address crawler protection and uses open signup and synthetic API keys. Never apply it to a normal deployment. It needs ports 3400/3402/3403, Docker, Python, pnpm and enough memory for the builds/local model. Override `M5_MODEL_PORT`/`M5_RESEARCH_PORT` if occupied and use those ports in the test commands.

PowerShell example:

```powershell
$m5Env = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'seoseo-m5check.env'
Copy-Item .env.example $m5Env
$env:POSTGRES_PASSWORD = 'disposable-m5check-only'
$env:WEB_PORT = '3400'
$env:WEB_BASE_URL = 'http://127.0.0.1:3400'
$env:SEOSEO_BACKEND_IMAGE = 'seoseo-backend:m5check'
$env:SEOSEO_WEB_IMAGE = 'seoseo-web:m5check'
docker build -t seoseo-backend:m5check backend
docker build -t seoseo-web:m5check frontend
$m5Args = @('-p','seoseo-m5check','-f','deploy/compose.yaml','-f','deploy/compose.m5-test.yaml','--env-file',$m5Env,'--profile','ollama')
```

markdown:
# SERP keyword clustering (KW-11)

The project's **Keywords** page offers **Group keywords into page topics**, an adjustable overlap threshold and CSV export. This is a read-only planning aid; grouping makes no external requests, stores no groups and changes no keywords or page assignments. Existing research and explicit SERP analyses populate the shared search cache.

## Evidence and grouping

The project scope is the union of saved keywords, research ideas, rank-tracker keywords and imported competitive-volume keywords in one country/language. It is deduplicated and bounded to the first 500 keywords alphabetically; the response reports the full scope size and sampled size. Another project's keyword list never enters this scope. Public SERP snapshots remain instance-wide shared cache data.

The newest snapshot per keyword/market is used. Only snapshots newer than seven days and distinct HTTP(S) URLs in positions 1–10 are eligible. Empty latest snapshots replace older evidence. URL parsing normalizes hosts/default ports and removes fragments; query strings, scheme, path case and trailing slash differences are preserved. Duplicate URLs do not increase overlap. Missing, stale/future and insufficient-result evidence is exposed separately, never interpreted as distinct search intent.

Every pair in a group must have the same provider and exactness flag and share at least min_shared URLs (2–10, default 3). Keywords are processed alphabetically and join the first compatible group. This deterministic complete-link rule prevents A/B and B/C overlap from implying an unsupported A/C match. It is conservative and order-defined, rather than an optimal partition or a claim of semantic identity. The representative is alphabetical, not chosen by volume or business importance. A group's minimum overlap is calculated over all member pairs. Ungrouped keywords had enough evidence but did not join a group at the selected threshold.

Each eligible keyword includes provider, exactness, snapshot time and the URL set used. Review groups and query differences before mapping to pages. Non-exact provider samples are clearly labelled aggregated results in the UI; they do not establish Google rankings.

## REST and MCP

`GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/keyword-clusters?country=US&language=en&min_shared=3`

Country and language default to the project. Normal project authorization applies: members can read, including archived projects; other tenants receive 404. Invalid market codes or an out-of-range threshold receive 422. The endpoint does not require configured provider credentials. No migration or worker is needed.

MCP `cluster_keywords` accepts project_id and the same optional market/threshold fields and calls the same service. The server now exposes 88 tools. The bundled clustering workflow uses this tool before recommending any additional SERP checks.

The response contains clusters, ungrouped, unavailable, scope/sample/eligible counts and warnings. CSV export uses the displayed response, includes grouped/ungrouped/unavailable keywords, provider, exactness, timestamp, market and minimum pair overlap. Formula-like cells are escaped. Opening an explicit keyword SERP analysis can make a provider request; closing it refreshes the clustering view.

## Verification

Backend tests cover complete-link chain prevention, deterministic ordering, provider/exactness separation, stale evidence, top-ten bounds, deduplication, conservative URL identity and empty scope. End-to-end fixtures additionally cover saved/research/rank/import scopes, latest empty snapshots, market/project/tenant isolation, member access, archived reads, threshold validation, the 500-keyword cap and REST/MCP parity.

Use a disposable password-auth stack with open signup and a DB container named with the `seoseo-m6check` prefix. The scripts create synthetic users/projects and directly insert fixtures with local psql; never target a normal deployment.

```powershell
$env:PUPPETEER_MODULE = 'PATH_TO_TEMP_INSTALL/node_modules/puppeteer-core'
```

title: Internal link graph and suggestions (SA-12)
markdown:
# Internal link graph and suggestions (SA-12)

Completed site audits now have an **Internal links** tab. It visualizes a selected page's incoming/outgoing neighborhood, exposes full stored-audit link counts, supports URL/title filtering and weak-link filtering, and exports the displayed evidence as JSON. Clicking a graph node or table URL selects the page; a page-detail link opens the existing audit inspection view. The diagram is keyboard accessible and scrolls within its container on smaller screens.

## Evidence and limits

`GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/audits/{audit_id}/internal-links?limit=200`

MCP `get_internal_link_graph` accepts project_id, audit_id and optional limit with the same semantics. Members can read, including archived projects. Other projects/tenants receive 404; unauthenticated callers receive 401. Only completed audits qualify (other statuses return 409). Limit is 10–500 (default 200), with invalid ranges returning 422. No migration, worker, provider credentials or fresh crawl is needed. Graph reads do not write or queue jobs.

The repository reads authorized audit metadata, nodes, counts and edges in one repeatable-read, read-only transaction. Pages are sampled alphabetically by URL, with ID as the tie-breaker. total_pages reports the full stored audit; sampled_pages reports the selected subset. Node title/H1 evidence is capped at 300 characters each.

For each selected page, incoming_sources counts distinct other source pages across the full audit. followed_incoming_sources requires at least one observed link without nofollow. outgoing_targets counts distinct non-self destinations; unfetched_targets counts destinations with no matching stored audit page. An unfetched destination is unknown, not necessarily broken. Counts are recomputed from link records rather than copied from potentially incomplete analysis metrics.

Edges connect only selected stored pages and exclude self-links. Duplicate source/target pairs become one edge with occurrences, an anchor sample (up to 200 characters) and followed=true if any observed link for the pair lacks nofollow. Full-audit counts can therefore exceed counts implied by the displayed edges. The response returns at most 5000 edges and exposes total_sample_edges and edges_truncated. Its page sample and edge limits are independent of the UI neighborhood display cap of six neighbors in each direction.

The audit itself is a bounded crawl. Zero observed incoming sources never proves website-wide orphan status. Early stop reasons, failed fetches, omitted sample pages and truncated graph edges have explicit warnings. Dashed edges mean nofollow-only observations, not a claim about how search engines value the link.

## Editorial suggestions

Sources and targets must be indexable HTTP 200 HTML pages without redirects, within the audit start host or its www twin. Both HTML and header canonical declarations, when present, must normalize to the page's own URL. The audited entry URL is not suggested as a target.

Targets have at most one observed followed incoming source across the full stored audit. Candidate pairs must share at least two distinct title/H1 terms (Unicode alphanumeric, at least three characters, excluding a small English stopword list). Existing edges—including nofollow-only pairs—and self-pairs are excluded. Terms are lexical evidence, not semantic intent, and the stopword list is not a multilingual language model.

Targets sort by fewest followed sources then URL; candidates sort by number of shared terms then source URL. Results are capped at three sources per target and fifty suggestions overall. Only selected sample pages participate. If the edge list is truncated, all suggestions are disabled because omitted edges might already connect a proposed pair. No suggested links are inserted into the site or database.

## Verification

Unit tests exercise eligibility, redirects/canonicals/status/indexability/scope, lexical overlap, existing nofollow/self-pair exclusion, entry-URL exclusion and edge-cap behavior. The API regression adds stored fixtures for full-audit counts from outside the sample, duplicates, self-links, unfetched targets, early-stop warnings, empty/noncompleted audits, a 5112-edge dense graph, tenant/project/member/archive isolation, REST/MCP parity and no job creation.

Use a disposable password-auth stack with open signup and a database container named with the seoseo-m6check prefix. These scripts create synthetic users/projects and directly insert fixtures using local psql; never point them at a normal deployment.

```powershell

$env:PUPPETEER_MODULE = 'PATH_TO_TEMP_INSTALL/node_modules/puppeteer-core'
node scripts/e2e-internal-links-browser.cjs http://127.0.0.1:3400 seoseo-m6check-db OUTPUT_DIRECTORY
python scripts/validate-agent-skills.py
pnpm --dir frontend typecheck
pnpm --dir frontend lint
pnpm --dir frontend build
```

The browser regression verifies the audit tab, interactive SVG/table selection, dashed nofollow style, page filter, sample-limit changes, JSON download, suggestions, no new crawl requests, desktop/mobile overflow and absence of browser errors. It saves screenshots for visual review.
