title: Audit comparison and scheduled re-audits (SA-13)
markdown:
# Audit comparison and scheduled re-audits (SA-13)

Completed audit results now have a **Compare** tab. Choose another completed audit of the same normalized start URL to inspect observed page and issue differences. The audit history page also has **Scheduled re-audits**, where an admin can review a completed audit's crawl settings and explicitly enable or disable recurring crawls.

## Comparison evidence

`GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/audits/{audit_id}/comparison?baseline_id=UUID`

MCP `compare_site_audits` accepts the same IDs plus kind, limit and offset. Both audits must belong to the current workspace/project and be completed. Different audits/start URLs are required. Members can read, including archived projects. Other-project/tenant IDs return 404; incomplete audits return 409; invalid comparison filters/ranges return 422.

One read-only repeatable-read transaction reads both audit records and at most 10,000 stored pages each. URLs are exact stored normalized identities; query strings and schemes remain distinct. Metadata field fingerprints compare full title/description/H1 values rather than truncated previews. Differences include status, fetch class, redirect state, title, meta description, H1, canonicals, indexability, content hash, word count, depth and inlinks where comparable.

The response distinguishes changed, unchanged, only_in_baseline and only_in_current observations. An absent URL is never automatically called deleted. Newly observed issues are distinguished from issues no longer observed on comparable successful HTML pages. If a page was not visited, failed, redirected or used different rendering/Lighthouse settings, absent prior issues are unconfirmed. A failed fetch does not turn its missing title/content into a content change or resolved issue. Unchanged means no comparable observed differences, not proof that the live page is identical.

Whole-audit health/issue totals remain visible in the baseline/current records, with a score delta only if both scores exist. Differences can reflect changed crawl coverage, configuration or analysis rules. Early stops, failed fetches and settings changes have explicit warnings. Comparison does not crawl, mutate data or queue jobs.

Kind defaults to changes (all except unchanged); other values are all, changed, unchanged, only_in_baseline and only_in_current. Limit is 1–500 (default 50), offset defaults to zero. Counts cover the full URL union; total_matching describes the selected filter before pagination. Pages sort by URL. The UI links to each observation's baseline/current page detail.

## Recurring crawls

`GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/audit-schedule` returns the current schedule or null.

`PUT /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/audit-schedule` and MCP `set_audit_schedule` require admin access. Supply expected_revision (0 for first configuration), expected_domain, baseline_audit_id, schedule, hour_utc and weekday. MCP `get_audit_schedule` reads the same record. Frequency is manual (disabled), daily, weekly, or monthly on day 1. Hours are UTC 0–23; weekdays are Monday=1 through Sunday=7. Next time is strictly in the future. The UI additionally displays the next occurrence in the viewer's local time.

Enabling requires an active project and a completed baseline auditing the current website host or its www twin. The service validates the URL policy, crawler limits and renderer availability and freezes that baseline's configuration. The form shows start URL, page budget, robots policy, rendering/Lighthouse and exclusions before saving. It does not start an immediate audit. Disabling an existing schedule needs no baseline and remains possible on archived projects. Revision checks prevent silent overwrites; reload after a 409 conflict.

Migration 0015 adds one schedule per project. The existing worker scheduler checks every sixty seconds. Under the same project row lock used by manual audit starts, it validates the due slot/revision and atomically commits the audit, job, next time and latest-audit pointer. Multiple workers cannot enqueue the same occurrence. Missed occurrences are not replayed as a backlog. An already queued/running audit skips the occurrence and advances to the next scheduled time, exposing the reason.

Archives, website identity changes, unavailable required rendering, invalid operator URL policy/settings and 100 retained project audits pause the schedule in manual mode with an explicit error. The cap never deletes existing audits; clean up unneeded history and explicitly re-enable. The last queued audit remains inspectable. The worker checks scheduled website authorization before starting and before each further crawl batch; queued runs for a changed/archived website stop with a recorded error. Requests already in flight can finish. A probe moving outside the reviewed host/www scope does not proceed with a full recurring crawl.

Frozen crawl budgets, robots policy and the existing guarded fetcher apply. Scheduled jobs reuse the normal durable crawler, checkpoints, retries and cancellation. Deleting the baseline audit clears its reference while retaining frozen settings; deleting the project cascades the schedule. Saving a new configuration preserves the historical last-run pointer as the last queued scheduled audit.

## Verification

Unit tests cover comparable versus missing/failed issue observations and changed collection methods. The disposable API regression additionally verifies full-value metadata changes, URL/status/configuration gates, filters/paging, tenant/project/member isolation, schedule revision races, admin controls, two-worker atomic claims, active-run skips, archive/domain/quota/renderer pauses, a queued website guard and a real three-page crawl of the local badseo fixture. All three MCP tools are checked against REST.

`scripts/e2e-audit-comparison.py API_ORIGIN M6CHECK_DB WORKER1 WORKER2` requires two created but stopped disposable worker containers; it starts both. Use a password-auth API with open signup, private crawler access and a dummy renderer URL; workers need private crawler access and no renderer. The local badseo nginx fixture must have the network alias audit-fixture.example. The renderer mismatch exercises safe schedule pausing without any browser rendering request. Container names must start with seoseo-m6check. Never use a normal deployment.

`scripts/e2e-audit-comparison-browser.cjs WEB_ORIGIN M6CHECK_DB OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` uses a temporary puppeteer-core installation through PUPPETEER_MODULE and local Chrome. It verifies baseline/filter controls, unknown absences, settings review, save/disable and desktop/mobile layouts. The test disables its recurring schedule before exiting.

Verified on 2026-11-13: all 86 workspace tests, Rust formatting, workspace/all-targets clippy with warnings denied, app build, frontend typecheck/lint/production build, the disposable API/two-worker/real-crawl regression and desktop/mobile browser checks passed. All 14 portable skills validate against 92 MCP tools. Screenshots were visually reviewed; comparison controls were corrected to keep narrow layouts within their container.

title: Stored evidence research: cannibalization and AI index (RT-07, AI-05)
markdown:
# Stored evidence research: cannibalization and AI index (RT-07, AI-05)

These read-only features use existing project data. They require no configured search/model provider, do not create jobs, and never call external engines. Members can read them, including archived projects. Another project or tenant's evidence is not included.

## Multi-URL candidates

The **Rank tracking** page now offers **Cannibalization candidates**. Choose a country/language and click **Find competing URLs** to see keywords where multiple distinct URLs from the project registrable domain appeared in the same cached search results. Each candidate includes best observed positions, provider, exactness and snapshot time.

`GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/cannibalization`

MCP `get_cannibalization_flags` accepts project_id and optional country, language, limit and offset. Market defaults to the project. Limit is 1–100 (default 25). The project website is required.

Scope is the existing union of saved/researched/tracked/imported keywords in the selected market, capped at the first 500 alphabetically. Full scope size, sampled, checked, matched and flagged counts remain visible independently of pagination. The newest snapshot within thirty days is authoritative, including empty result sets. Only positions 1–30 participate. URL parsing normalizes hosts/default ports, removes fragments and rejects credentials/non-HTTP(S) URLs; query strings and distinct paths remain separate. Duplicate results collapse to one URL at its best position. Actual result URL hosts must belong to the project registrable domain, including subdomains; a provider's domain field alone is not trusted.

Multiple useful search results from one site can be legitimate. Candidates do not establish harmful cannibalization, simultaneous competition in Google when the provider is aggregated, or a reason to merge pages automatically. Unchecked/stale keyword evidence remains unknown. Review intent and page purpose before editing.

## Your prompt and brand index

The **AI visibility** page now has **Your prompt and brand index**. Search retained successful answer text by literal brand, optionally filter saved prompt text by topic, and choose saved prompts or answer excerpts. Market controls apply to the frozen run country/language, not the current model configuration. The index remains usable when model providers are no longer configured.

`GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/ai-index`

Optional parameters: view=prompts (default) or answers, brand (1–80 characters), topic (1–120), country, language, limit (1–100, default 25) and nonnegative offset. Blank/control-character search terms and invalid ranges/markets receive 422. Omit brand/topic to browse the retained index.

MCP `explore_ai_prompts` returns grouped saved prompts with optional brand/topic filters. MCP `lookup_ai_brand` requires a brand and returns matching successful saved-answer excerpts. Neither generates prompts or calls models. This is the project's own retained evidence, not a global prompt-demand or consumer-chat database.

The repository joins the current project website identity to its trackers, then expands frozen run prompts/models into expected answer cells. Deleted history and previous-website trackers are outside the index. Saved answers from incomplete/failed runs remain valid observations; failed cells and unattempted cells are reported separately. Extra answer rows outside a frozen run configuration do not enter its denominator.

Summary counts describe the selected market/topic scope before filtering to brand matches. Mention rates use successful saved answer cells only and stay null with no successful observations or no requested brand. A failed/unattempted cell is not a measured absence. Grouped prompts count matching retained runs and expected/successful/failed/unchecked cells. Brand-filtered prompt results require at least one matching saved answer; unfiltered prompt browsing also includes prompts with no saved successful answer.

Brand terms are regex-escaped and matched case-insensitively with alphanumeric boundaries. Topic filters use literal case-insensitive substrings, escaping LIKE wildcard characters. Input does not become a regex or SQL expression. Answer excerpts are capped at 500 characters around the first literal-boundary match (or the beginning when browsing without a brand). Engine, grounding, timestamp and gateway fingerprint preserve provenance. Text-only answers remain text-only observations. Queries share a repeatable-read read-only snapshot so summary, totals and paged results are consistent.

## Verification

`scripts/e2e-evidence-research.py API_ORIGIN M6CHECK_DB` seeds synthetic SERP/model-answer evidence in a disposable password-auth/open-signup stack. It checks duplicates/fragments, foreign URLs, stale/empty/depth evidence, scoped counts, success/failure/unchecked denominators, literal/Unicode matching, regex and LIKE escaping, frozen markets, previous websites, project/tenant/member/archive isolation, paging, all three MCP tools and absence of new jobs. Database names must start with seoseo-m6check; never run against a normal deployment.

`scripts/e2e-evidence-research-browser.cjs WEB_ORIGIN M6CHECK_DB OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` uses a temporary puppeteer-core installation through PUPPETEER_MODULE and local Chrome. It verifies source/position labels, brand/prompt controls, denominators and excerpts, desktop/mobile layouts and no new SERP/model calls. It saves screenshots for visual review.

title: Homepage technology and sampled link prospects (DO-06, BL-07)
markdown:
# Homepage technology and sampled link prospects (DO-06, BL-07)

## Homepage technology hints

The **Competitive** page now offers an explicit **Inspect homepage technology** action. It observes public markup for WordPress, Next.js, Nuxt and Shopify hints. Results identify fingerprints, not verified technology versions, backend services, vulnerabilities or a complete stack. A site may customize or hide these hints, and another site can imitate them.

`POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/technology` / MCP `detect_technologies`

Input accepts an optional homepage URL or hostname; the project's HTTPS root is the default. Authorization precedes shared-cache or network access. HTTP(S) roots only: no credentials, non-root path, query parameters or custom ports. The normal URL/IP/DNS guard applies; private access remains an explicit operator-only test setting. Custom ports are rejected before normalization.

The lookup uses an honest SeoSeoBot User-Agent and checks exact robots.txt first. Only successful plain/non-HTML robots or missing robots (404/410) permit proceeding. Disallow, blocks, rate limits, inconclusive access or crawl delays over five seconds stop the lookup. Short declared delays are respected. It then fetches one exact homepage with a 1 MiB body cap and ten-second request timeouts. Redirects are returned as observations without following them. Bot challenges stop without retries, cookie handshakes, browser impersonation or bypasses. Referenced assets are inspected as markup strings; they are not downloaded or executed.

Meta-generator declarations and selected script/link/image asset paths are parsed as structured HTML rather than searched in article text. Shopify asset hosts must match exactly, not a lookalike suffix. Signals are fixed labels, with at most four per supported platform. Raw HTML, cookies, response headers and asset-query tokens are not retained.

Positive, unknown, redirected, robots-disallowed and blocked records are cached for 24 hours by canonical homepage URL. Cache hits make no network requests. Database-backed one-minute project and URL cooldown claims bound concurrent uncached requests without holding a connection while fetching. A crashed lookup's claim expires; there is no user refresh bypass. Unknown/empty results do not prove technology absence.

The signature references are the official descriptions of [WordPress content directories](https://developer.wordpress.org/advanced-administration/wordpress/wp-config/), [Next.js asset prefixes](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/assetPrefix), [Nuxt build asset directories](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/blob/main/docs/4.api/6.nuxt-config.md) and [Shopify CDN assets](https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/themes/best-practices/performance/use-shopify-cdn). These paths can be customized or moved; they support hints only.

## Link-intersect prospects

The **Backlinks** page lets a member choose one to five accessible competitor projects, including archived projects, and compare their current-website backlink samples with this project's samples. Create competitor projects and use existing discovery/import workflows to populate evidence first. No new discovery, contact lookup, outreach or messages occur during comparison.

`POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/link-intersect` / MCP `find_link_intersect`

Input fields: competitor_project_ids, optional min_competitors (default 1, at most the number selected), limit (1–100, default 25), offset (nonnegative). IDs must be distinct, exclude this project, and belong to the current workspace. All selected sites need distinct registrable domains; duplicate aliases of the same site are rejected. Another tenant/project outside the caller's scope returns 404. Website identities are rechecked inside a read-only repeatable-read transaction; a concurrent website change returns 409.

For each current website, the repository selects the latest snapshot per dataset/source, including empty snapshots. It then samples the ten newest dataset/source snapshots per project. Historical website snapshots and lost sample rows are excluded. Scope metadata exposes available/sample dataset counts and snapshot date ranges; absent or omitted evidence has explicit warnings.

Prospects are referring source domains seen in at least the selected number of competitor samples and not seen in the current site's selected samples. The current site's own registrable domain is excluded. Competitor counts deduplicate project IDs; observed links deduplicate project/source/target pairs across datasets. At most three source URLs per prospect are returned, with verified/imported evidence counts and newest sample time. Category counts can overlap when one pair has evidence in multiple datasets. Results sort by competitor count then source domain; total counts remain independent of pagination.

“Not observed in these samples” does not establish that the live site lacks a link. Imported and inconclusive observations are not independent verification. This is a bounded free-first link-intersect workflow over user-imported and guarded-discovery evidence, not an exhaustive Common Crawl or commercial backlink index. Review source relevance and live evidence before any outreach.

## Verification and related fixes

The parser regression distinguishes actual generator/asset markup from article text and lookalike hosts. The disposable API regression additionally checks robots/bot/redirect stops, positive/negative cache hits with no extra requests, concurrent cooldown claims, URL bounds, scoped latest/empty backlink samples, baseline exclusion, dataset caps, identities, tenant/member/archive access, paging, MCP parity and no jobs.

```powershell
python scripts/e2e-tech-and-prospects.py http://127.0.0.1:3401 seoseo-m6check-db seoseo-m6check-tech-fixture
$env:PUPPETEER_MODULE = 'PATH_TO_TEMP_INSTALL/node_modules/puppeteer-core'
node scripts/e2e-tech-and-prospects-browser.cjs http://127.0.0.1:3400 seoseo-m6check-db OUTPUT_DIRECTORY
```

These scripts require a disposable password-auth/open-signup API with private crawler access and the nginx fixture at deploy/test/m6-tech/nginx.conf. Give the fixture aliases good.tech-fixture.example, robots.tech-fixture.example, bot.tech-fixture.example, robotblock.tech-fixture.example, redirect.tech-fixture.example and cooldown.tech-fixture.example. Only container names beginning with seoseo-m6check are accepted. Never target a normal deployment. The script resets only technology-cache keys in that disposable database when rerun.

Browser verification covers explicit homepage hints/cache, competitor/minimum selection, imported provenance, sample dates, desktop/mobile layouts and no discovery jobs. Deferred pages now wait for a stable client-ready fallback before reading layout-populated query cache, preventing hydration mismatches. Discovery/import component keys are unique.

Testing also found and corrected the crawler normalizer's custom-port bug: Url already removes default ports, while port_or_known_default also returns explicit custom ports. Custom ports now remain part of URL identity. Existing stored audit records are unchanged; the regression verifies explicit port 8080 is retained. Homepage technology lookup still rejects custom ports intentionally.

Implementation checkpoint: REST, MCP and the audit-page card are present. Real-provider and browser acceptance remain pending; no real API key was used.

The server operator can set optional `CRUX_API_KEY` in `.env` and recreate the API service. Enable the Chrome UX Report API for that free Google Cloud key. The key stays server-side. `CRUX_API_URL` is an operator-only fixture/proxy override, outside project input.


The service calls the fixed upstream API, never the supplied website. Public positive/negative records are cached for 24 hours by operator endpoint, scope, target and device. # Bing Webmaster Tools

M6 IN-04 connects a project to Bing's first-party Webmaster data without making the installation operator register a shared OAuth client. An administrator enters a user-generated Bing Webmaster API key in Integrations. The server validates the key with `GetUserSites` before encrypting it with `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`; replacement is atomic and clears the prior site selection. The plaintext key is never stored or serialized.

The credential remains project-bound even though Bing issues API keys per user. Only administrators can list account-wide sites, and they can select only an exact verified site returned by Bing. Members can read the selected site's top queries, top pages, daily crawl statistics and paged inbound-link counts. Verification codes, provider type metadata and provider error bodies are removed. Calls have a 20-second timeout, no redirects and a 4 MiB response limit. Bing's weekly top-query/page results and sampled link counts are explicitly not presented as exhaustive or real-time.

REST endpoints live under `/api/v1/projects/{project_id}/bing`; MCP exposes `list_bing_webmaster_sites`, `set_bing_webmaster_site`, and `get_bing_webmaster_report`. The dashboard remains the only place to enter or replace the secret. `BING_WEBMASTER_API_URL` is an operator-only fixture/proxy override; project input cannot redirect credentials to another host.

Validation includes strict workspace Clippy, OpenAPI operation-id checks, frontend type checking/linting, and `scripts/e2e-bing.py`. The disposable regression verifies tenant isolation, validation before save, encrypted storage, verification-secret stripping, exact verified-site selection, all four REST report kinds, MCP reads, link paging and disconnect. Live-provider acceptance still requires a user's Bing key and verified site.

Microsoft documents both OAuth and user API keys, and recommends OAuth for delegated third-party applications. The self-hosted first delivery uses the API-key option to avoid a global application registration while preserving per-project isolation. The integration uses Bing's JSON service, not the SOAP or POX protocols Microsoft retired on 31 August 2026.

References: [Bing Webmaster API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/bingwebmaster/), [getting API access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/bingwebmaster/getting-access), [OAuth scopes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/bingwebmaster/oauth2), [query statistics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.bing.webmaster.api.interfaces.iwebmasterapi.getquerystats), [inbound-link counts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.bing.webmaster.api.interfaces.iwebmasterapi.getlinkcounts).

title: Local business discovery, scans and city context
markdown:
# Local business discovery, scans and city context

Use the project **Local SEO** page to find an OpenStreetMap business, save a tracker with 1–50 unique keywords, and preview a 3×3, 5×5, 7×7 or 9×9 grid with 0.1–10 km point spacing. There are at most ten trackers per project. Discovery is explicit, cached for 30 days, attributed, and globally paced to one uncached request per second; it is never used for autocomplete or grid scans. The curated category list is not Google's taxonomy. Operators can change `NOMINATIM_URL` to an approved alternative endpoint.

## Rank collection and evidence imports

If discovery has no match, expand **Enter business details manually** and supply a verified name, address and coordinates. This saves an explicitly manual business identity without a lookup or rank request. Supply the separate exact Google provider ID when starting a scan.

Configure **Settings → Data providers → SerpApi (Maps and AI Overviews)** with an encrypted BYOK key and enable it explicitly. Collection is off by default and is separate from organic SERP fallback. Saving a tracker makes no rank requests.

A scan freezes the tracker geometry, selected saved keywords, country/language, exact target provider ID, depth, requester and source. Review the budget before starting: keywords × grid points, at most 250 cells. One scan can be active per tracker, and twenty runs can be retained; delete old inactive runs to free space. A durable worker queries the first Google Maps result page at each point at zoom 14, with the requested search-origin coordinates. This is a provider sample, not an exhaustive list of nearby businesses. See [SerpApi Maps documentation](https://serpapi.com/google-maps-api).

Enter the exact Google `place_id` (or `data_id` when the response has no place ID). It is different from the OSM ID. No fuzzy name matching is used. Each response retains returned positions and identities, up to 20 competitors. A successful response with no target means not returned in that sample; a failed or unchecked point remains unknown.

The worker records a cell attempt before making its request. On crash recovery, recorded cells are skipped, including an interrupted request whose result was not saved. This keeps retries from spending twice on the same cell; interrupted cells stay unknown. A provider failure stops the remaining scan, including 429, access rejection and malformed results. There is no retry around a block. The worker rechecks project access, requester membership and provider configuration before collection. Terminal queue failures are reconciled to failed scans while retaining evidence.

The free path is **Import local observations**. Supply source-labelled measured results from an export or manual observation; no provider requests or paid key are needed. The server validates saved keywords, grid bounds, dates, unique cell coordinates, unique competitor IDs/positions, depth and safe website links. Imports commit their status and cells atomically. Omitted cells stay unchecked.

```json
{
  "target_business_id": "example-place-id",
  "keywords": ["coffee"],
  "depth": 20,
  "observed_at": "2026-11-01T00:00:00Z",
  "source_note": "Manual Google Maps observation at the frozen grid point",
  "cells": [{
    "keyword": "coffee", "row": 0, "column": 0, "measured": true,
    "checked_at": "2026-11-01T00:00:00Z", "error": null,
    "results": [{"position": 2, "business_id": "example-place-id", "name": "Cafe", "address": null, "website": null}]
  }]
}
```

## Reading maps and metrics

Select a saved run and keyword. The accessible heatmap and optional MapLibre map distinguish ranks 1–3, 4–10, 11–20, not returned, and unchecked/failed points. Clicking a point shows that cell's competitors. Source, timestamp, status, depth and coverage remain visible. JSON export includes frozen configuration and evidence.

- **ARP**: mean position among points where the target was found; unknown if never found.
- **ATRP**: mean over measured points, assigning depth+1 to non-returned targets. This is an explicit penalty, not an observed rank.
- **SoLV**: percentage of measured points where the target was in the top three.

Failed and unchecked points are excluded from all metric denominators. Always compare coverage and identical grids, keywords, depths and sources. Missing evidence is not a zero score or verified ranking loss.

The geographic map loads only on explicit display. It uses [OpenStreetMap tiles](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/) with visible attribution, browser caching and referrer, no bulk download or offline prefetch. Set Compose `MAP_TILE_URL` and rebuild web, or set build-time `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_TILE_URL`, to choose an approved tile template (`none` disables base tiles for offline browser QA). The numeric grid works without tiles or WebGL.

The frontend dev/build scripts copy the installed MapLibre worker and its shared module into ignored `public/maplibre` assets. The map explicitly uses this same-origin, version-matched worker because bundling relocates MapLibre's entry module.

## City demand context (KW-10)

Import a source export through the Local SEO page or REST/MCP. Provide city, source/method, start/end dates and up to 500 unique keyword rows. Each row can contain explicit city searches/month, national searches/month and/or a normalized city relative-interest value from 0–100. An empty city search count remains null; an explicit zero remains zero. Relative interest is not search volume and is comparable only within the source export's normalization. National volume is never multiplied into an invented city estimate.

City datasets are scoped to the current project website, country and language. Changing those hides older data; restoring the exact scope restores retained data. The most recent 100 datasets per research kind are retained across website identities. Importing does not replace saved-keyword volume or trigger external collection.

## API and MCP

All REST endpoints are under `/api/v1`:

- `GET /local/categories`
- `POST /projects/{project_id}/local/businesses/search`
- `GET/POST /projects/{project_id}/local-trackers`
- `GET /projects/{project_id}/local-trackers/{tracker_id}/grid`
- `GET/POST /projects/{project_id}/local-trackers/{tracker_id}/scans`
- `POST /projects/{project_id}/local-trackers/{tracker_id}/scans/import`
- `GET/DELETE /projects/{project_id}/local-trackers/{tracker_id}/scans/{run_id}`
- `GET/POST /projects/{project_id}/city-demand`

MCP tools: `list_local_categories`, `search_local_businesses`, `create_local_tracker`, `list_local_trackers`, `get_local_grid_preview`, `start_local_scan`, `import_local_scan`, `list_local_scans`, `get_local_scan`, `import_city_demand`, `list_city_demand`. Writes require member role; every operation checks project access. Live start requires an exact reviewed request count; use saved history for read-only research.

Provider endpoints are fixed defaults or operator environment settings; project input cannot supply endpoints. `SERPAPI_URL` exists only for operator-approved proxies and offline fixtures. See [M6 acceptance](27-m6-acceptance.md).

title: Google AI Overview observations (AI-06)
markdown:
# Google AI Overview observations (AI-06)

The **AI visibility → Google AI Overviews** card captures an observed Google search summary and its reported citations. It is separate from generated model answer comparisons: no model creates an overview on Google's behalf.

For live collection, explicitly enable **SerpApi (Maps and AI Overviews)** and save your own key in Settings → Data providers. Keys use the existing encrypted workspace provider store and are never included in responses, jobs or logs. The key is optional: saved search evidence can be imported without a paid key.

Collection uses the project's current country/language, a keyword and optional search location. Review the maximum of two requests: one Google search, followed by at most one Google AI Overview token continuation. Tokens expire quickly and are used immediately, never stored or exposed. Provider continuation URLs are never followed; the fixed operator endpoint is used for both requests. A 24-hour project/website/market/keyword/location cache reuses captured data, and durable per-query cooldowns limit repeated requests. API calls time out, disable redirects, bound streamed responses to 2 MiB and sanitize upstream failures. There are no automatic scheduled requests.

Capture distinguishes:

- **present**: usable returned overview text, with reported citations.
- **absent**: a successful search response did not contain an overview. This is a single observation, not a claim about all users or future searches.
- **incomplete**: an overview envelope exists without usable text, such as an unresolved continuation. Presence/absence remains unknown.

A network/provider error is an error, never observed absence. Source links are limited to HTTP(S) URLs without credentials. They are reported citations, not verified support. Rendering uses plain React text and normal links; no provider HTML is inserted. Only normalized text (up to 20,000 characters), up to 50 citations, source/date and search context are retained; metadata and tokens are discarded. The most recent 100 observations per project/research kind are retained across website identities. History is visible only for the current project website/country/language.

REST under `/api/v1/projects/{project_id}`:

- `GET /ai-overviews`: retained observations in the current scope.
- `POST /ai-overviews`: keyword, optional location, expected_max_requests=2.
- `POST /ai-overviews/import`: keyword, optional location, observed_at, source_note and a SerpApi-format search response.

MCP tools: `capture_google_ai_overview`, `import_google_ai_overview`, `list_google_ai_overviews`. Writes require member role and project access. The UI shows history, provenance, status, citations, cache/request counts and JSON export.

Example evidence import:

```json
{
  "keyword": "what is coffee",
  "observed_at": "2026-11-01T00:00:00Z",
  "source_note": "Saved Google search response from the stated market",
  "response": {"ai_overview": {
    "text_blocks": [{"snippet": "Observed summary text"}],
    "references": [{"title": "Source", "link": "https://example.com/source"}]
  }}
}
```

Official provider contracts: [Google search AI Overview results](https://serpapi.com/ai-overview) and [token continuation API](https://serpapi.com/google-ai-overview-api). Reproducible fixture and browser validation are recorded in [M6 acceptance](27-m6-acceptance.md). Live collection still requires the operator's real provider credentials.

# M7 assistant and content foundation

The project **Assistant** tab adds private conversations, tool evidence, content briefs and draft term coverage. This records the initial M7 delivery. Its streaming and reviewed-memory follow-ups are implemented in [Assistant streaming and reviewed memory](29-assistant-streaming-and-memory.md). The remaining milestone features are completed in [M7 operations and acceptance](30-m7-operations-and-acceptance.md).

## Configuration and privacy

Configure the same existing model settings on API and worker: `AI_OLLAMA_URL` + `AI_OLLAMA_MODELS` for free local inference, or `OPENAI_COMPAT_BASE_URL` + `LLM_MODEL` (optionally `AI_VISIBILITY_MODELS` and `OPENAI_COMPAT_API_KEY`) for a compatible gateway. Pull an instruction-following model into Ollama first. Use a context window of at least 16k tokens. JSON-object response mode must be supported. Native Anthropic/Gemini visibility engines are excluded from the assistant.

The selected model receives project identity/market, bounded canonical memory/tool evidence and up to eight prior completed turns. Each history message/answer caps at 1,000 characters; evidence objects cap at 6,000 characters with labelled truncated previews. External gateways receive the same data when selected. Chats are private to the authenticated user, including API keys/OAuth acting as that user. Admins do not automatically see other users' chats. Draft coverage runs locally without sending drafts to a model.

Endpoints/keys come only from operator configuration. Model requests follow no redirects/proxies, time out after 45 seconds and cap responses at 128 KiB. Malformed, truncated, blocked and rate-limited responses fail visibly.

## Read-only tools and lifecycle

Messages enqueue durable single-attempt `assistant_turn` jobs and return 202. The UI polls queued/running turns and resumes after refresh. Progress also appears in Jobs. Each model response selects one JSON action:

| Tool | Evidence |
|---|---|
| `project_memory` | Canonical context/key pages/research notes; injected before the first call |
| `audit_summary` | Latest completed audit matching the project website |
| `rank_movers` | Comparable numeric position changes from the current website/market dashboard sample |
| `cached_serp` | Up to ten titles/snippets within seven days in the project market; provider/exactness/time included |

Models cannot select tenant identities or URLs to fetch. Unknown tools produce evidence errors; unexpected action fields fail closed. There is no shell, fetch, mutation or arbitrary MCP dispatch. Stored data can influence answer quality but cannot grant extra capabilities. Answers render as plain text.

Each turn permits four additional tool actions/five model calls. Intent persists before model access; ambiguous requests are never replayed. Lease reaping fails crashed single-attempt jobs, and reads/new sends reconcile failed turns. Saved evidence survives errors; retry requires a new message.

Limits: 20 chats/user/project; 40 turns/chat; one active turn/chat; four active turns/workspace; 4,000 characters/message. Project/workspace locks serialize quotas and queue insertion. Chats freeze website/country/language. Changes/archival prevent continuation and invalidate active work before another model request/final answer. History retains its original scope. Workers recheck membership before requests. Deletion removes prompts/answers/evidence; job payloads contain IDs only. Already submitted model requests cannot be recalled.

## Content

Briefs require a nonempty SERP cached within seven days in the project market. They open a private assistant conversation with an editorial request for audience/intent assumptions, title/outline/questions, links from saved key pages, sources and evidence gaps. They do not publish, save reports, refresh SERPs or write memory. Recommendations need editorial review; snippets do not establish full competitor content.

Coverage uses tokens appearing in at least two distinct top-ten titles/snippets. It removes common English/Indonesian stop words and numeric tokens, selects up to 30 by reference frequency/lexical order, and returns the percentage present in the draft using case-insensitive whole-token matching. Missing evidence/no repeated terms yields `null`; measured zero overlap yields `0`. Matching works best in languages with spaces; word count uses whitespace. This is a lexical editorial hint, not quality or ranking prediction. Sources, exactness, market, time and references remain visible.

## REST and MCP

Authenticated project paths start at `/api/v1/projects/{project_id}`:

| Method/path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| GET `/assistant/models` | Models and disclosure |
| GET/POST `/assistant/chats` | List/create caller's chats |
| GET/DELETE `/assistant/chats/{chat_id}` | Read/delete caller's chat |
| POST `/assistant/chats/{chat_id}/messages` | Queue `{model,message}`; 202 |
| POST `/content/brief` | Queue `{keyword,model}`; 202/private chat |
| POST `/content/score` | Local `{keyword,content}` coverage |

MCP adds `create_content_brief`, `score_page_content`, `get_assistant_chat` (118 tools). Poll the private chat until its final turn is completed/failed.

## Verification

Migration `0019_assistant.sql` is additive. Run workspace fmt/clippy/tests, frontend lint/typecheck/build and API generation. Build the debug app with backend mounted at `/src` and `seoseo-target` at `/src/target`, then run `docker compose -p seoseo-m7check -f deploy/compose.m7check.yaml up -d --build` and `python scripts/e2e-assistant.py http://127.0.0.1:3501 seoseo-m7check-db-1`.

Test Compose does not read production `.env`; loopback ports are 3500 web, 3501 API, 3502 offline model. Optional `ollama` reuses the external `seoseo-m5-ollama-models` volume; pass `M7_OLLAMA_MODELS` explicitly. Fixtures verify contracts/isolation, not model intelligence or live search.

Verified 2026-11-14 (Asia/Jakarta):

- Workspace fmt and clippy with warnings denied passed. All 101 workspace unit tests and doc tests passed, including action parsing, instruction/data roles, evidence truncation, missing metrics and whole-token coverage.
- Frontend lint, typecheck and production build passed; Docker web image built and standalone Compose started successfully. Generated OpenAPI matched the built binary byte-for-byte. The 14 portable skills validate against 118 MCP tools. Generated third-party MapLibre assets are excluded from lint.
- `e2e-assistant.py` passed against a disposable password-auth database: ownership/tenant/auth, strict input validation, tool evidence/history, unknown tools, forbidden identity arguments, provider failures without retry, tool budget, interrupted work, cached briefs, null/zero/full coverage, market isolation, concurrent chat quotas, deleted-chat outstanding job budget, API-key/MCP parity and deletion.
- `e2e-assistant-browser.cjs` passed desktop and 390px mobile flows with no page errors or horizontal overflow: chat creation/send, reload/history selection, expanded evidence, missing/100% coverage, queued brief and malformed-model failure. It caught and fixed a new-chat text-clearing race. Screenshots were visually reviewed.
- Real `ollama/qwen2.5:1.5b` completed an in-app turn using canonical memory and correctly answered that the fixture business provides technical SEO audits for small businesses. This confirms local inference through the actual worker/UI path, not just a fixture. Early small-model tool loops prompted separating server policy into the system role and an explicit final-response instruction; loop failure remains bounded and visible.

Browser command: `PUPPETEER_MODULE=PATH_TO_TEMP_INSTALL/node_modules/puppeteer-core node scripts/e2e-assistant-browser.cjs http://127.0.0.1:3500 seoseo-m7check-db-1 OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ollama/qwen2.5:1.5b`. `CHROME_PATH` optionally selects Chrome. QA artifacts for this run remain outside the repository at `C:/Users/jamal/AppData/Local/Temp/seoseo-m7-browser/qa-verified`.

This records the initial delivery on `codex/m7-assistant-content`. Subsequent streaming/reviewed memory and the completed weekly digest exit criterion are documented in the linked follow-up guides.

title: Assistant streaming and reviewed memory
markdown:
# Assistant streaming and reviewed memory

This completes AG-01's streaming and reviewed memory follow-ups from the [initial assistant delivery](28-assistant-and-content.md). Subsequent alerts, weekly digests and the remaining milestone features are complete; see [M7 operations and acceptance](30-m7-operations-and-acceptance.md).

## Streamed answers

The worker requests real streamed chat completions from the same approved Ollama/compatible model. The bounded SSE decoder accepts arbitrary transport/UTF-8 boundaries, CRLF, comments and multiline data. It requires both a normal `stop` finish and `[DONE]`. Truncation, malformed packets, unsupported native tool calls/refusals, timeouts and interrupted streams fail the turn without replaying inference. Limits are 45 seconds/request, 1 MiB of wire data, 128 KiB/packet and 20,000 characters/action. Existing five-call/four-tool budgets remain.

The assistant still validates complete JSON actions. While a canonical final action streams (`type` first, `answer` second), it decodes complete string prefixes and persists the draft at most four times/second. Incomplete escapes and Unicode surrogate pairs stay buffered. Other field orders still validate at completion but do not expose partial text. Tool actions and proposed memory notes are not rendered as answer drafts. Drafts are explicitly labelled incomplete; final validation replaces them with the completed answer. Failure clears the draft, and crash reconciliation clears interrupted drafts. No synthetic character animation or extra inference call is used.

`GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/assistant/chats/{chat_id}/turns/{turn_id}/events` emits `turn` events containing private turn snapshots. Ownership and workspace membership are checked at entry and throughout the connection. Responses use `Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform`, `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, and keepalives. `no-transform` is required to prevent Next.js compression from buffering partial events until completion; direct API tests alone do not catch that problem. Connections close after terminal status or about 45 seconds, before the existing HTTP timeout. Browser EventSource reconnects to stored state; it never starts a model request. If access ends, an `unavailable` event closes the connection. The UI retains polling as a disconnected-stream fallback, closes subscriptions on chat changes/unmount, and restores persisted drafts after reload/chat selection.

## Reviewed memory notes

A final action may propose an optional plain-text `memory_note` of at most 2,000 characters. Instructions ask the model to propose one only when the user requests remembering information. This is an unsaved suggestion; even an unsolicited model proposal cannot modify memory.

The caller sees **Review memory note**, can edit the note and inspect current memory/recent notes, then explicitly selects **Save reviewed note**. Workspace admins/owners can save their own chat's proposal. Members can chat and view their own proposals, but cannot save them, matching the existing canonical-memory permission. No assistant tool performs writes, and no report/content publication is implied.

`POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/assistant/chats/{chat_id}/turns/{turn_id}/memory` accepts `{revision,note}` using normal authentication and cookie CSRF rules. The server appends a research-log entry through the existing canonical memory service; sections, competitors, key pages and unchanged section authors are preserved. Proposal scope must still match the active project website/country/language. Archived projects, another user's chat, non-completed/failed turns, missing proposals and already saved proposals are rejected.

Memory revision checking, the append, and marking the proposal applied occur in one transaction under the project/turn locks. Concurrent/repeated approvals cannot append twice. A stale revision returns 409 without changes; the UI offers **Reload memory for review** and requires another save action. The original model proposal and actual edited saved note remain distinct; the turn records `memory_applied_revision` and `memory_saved_note`. No model inference is invoked by review or approval.

## Migration and validation

Migration `0020_assistant_stream_memory.sql` adds only draft/proposal/approval fields. API/worker must run matching code and migrations. Regenerate OpenAPI/TypeScript as usual. MCP remains at 118 tools; `get_assistant_chat` includes the added draft/proposal state, and the existing canonical memory tools remain available to authorized external clients. Approval is an explicit UI/REST action rather than an automatically callable model tool.

The disposable stack and regression commands are documented in [the initial delivery](28-assistant-and-content.md). The model fixture now emits real SSE packets, delayed partials and interrupted streams. API coverage includes observable draft-before-completion, private SSE access, failure cleanup, no automatic memory write, editable approvals, role/ownership enforcement, stale revisions, repeated/concurrent approvals and changed-market rejection. Browser coverage includes the streaming draft and explicit review/edit/save flow.

Verified 2026-11-15 (Asia/Jakarta):

- All 103 workspace unit tests and doc tests passed. Workspace fmt/clippy with warnings denied and frontend lint/typecheck passed. The Docker frontend production build and standalone Compose startup passed.
- The expanded API regression passed streaming drafts before completion, private SSE access, interruption cleanup, reviewed/edited notes, stale/repeated/concurrent approvals, ownership/role enforcement and changed-market rejection, alongside the existing assistant/content checks.
- Desktop and 390px mobile browser checks passed streaming through the real Next proxy, proposal review/edit/explicit save, no automatic memory write, unchanged original sections, history reload, content coverage/briefs, visible model errors and no page errors/overflow. Screenshots were visually reviewed.
- Real `ollama/qwen2.5:1.5b` completed a streamed in-app answer using canonical memory that included the newly reviewed note. Fixture tests establish failure contracts; the Ollama check separately establishes actual local model access.

QA artifacts for this delivery: `C:/Users/jamal/AppData/Local/Temp/seoseo-m7-browser/qa-stream-memory-verified`. The normal local stack was not rebuilt during that acceptance. Subsequent milestone completion and deployment-specific limits are recorded in [M7 operations and acceptance](30-m7-operations-and-acceptance.md).

# M7 operations and acceptance

M7 is complete as of 2026-11-15 (Asia/Jakarta). [Assistant/content](28-assistant-and-content.md) and [streaming/reviewed memory](29-assistant-streaming-and-memory.md) cover AG-01..03. This delivery completes movement alerts, key-page monitoring, destinations, built-in reports/PDF, weekly email, business records, backup/restore and account deletion. The server exposes 121 MCP tools.

## Alerts and destinations

Open a project's **Alerts** tab. An admin chooses a position threshold (1–100), entering/leaving measured depth, and up to 100 exact-host key-page URLs. Settings use revision checks; reload after a concurrent-edit conflict. Changing project domain/market requires saving settings for the new scope. Enabling alerts considers subsequently completed observations, without backfilling old runs or calling providers. Schedule rank tracking and re-audits separately to collect observations.

The worker evaluates stored observations every minute. A manual evaluation uses the same domain service. Rank comparisons require adjacent completed runs from the same tracker, provider, exactness and measured depth. A null position means outside that measured depth, not position zero; absent result rows are unknown. Key pages compare completed audits with the same start URL and render mode, considering successful HTML pages without redirects. Missing/failed pages are incomparable. Title, description, canonical, robots and indexability changes are recorded. Each evaluation retains comparable/unavailable counts; event details contain at most 100 changed items. The feed supports acknowledgement and pagination.

An evaluation, immutable event and delivery jobs commit together. Unique source keys prevent concurrent evaluations from duplicating alerts. The scheduler rotates through up to 1,000 eligible projects per tick, processing up to 20 sources per project; large backlogs drain over subsequent ticks.

Admins can add up to ten generic webhook, Slack or Discord incoming-webhook destinations. Secret URLs are encrypted with `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`; reads return only name/type/host/state. Public HTTPS is required, with DNS filtering, no proxy and no redirects. Slack and Discord require their official webhook paths. Slack formatting escapes mention syntax; Discord disables mention parsing. Tests are limited to three per minute per destination. `NOTIFY_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true` exists solely for trusted disposable transport tests and is not forwarded by normal Compose.

Delivery is **single attempt**: an atomic transition to `sending` precedes network I/O. Timeouts, crashes, HTTP errors and ambiguous disconnects are visible in delivery history and never automatically replayed. This avoids duplicate external messages at the cost of possible missed delivery. Disabling/removing a destination, changing its revision, archiving/changing project scope, or disabling a subscription cancels stale queued work. Members see only their own email deliveries; admins can inspect project history.

## Weekly email

Set identical operator configuration on API and worker:

```dotenv
SMTP_HOST=smtp.example.com
SMTP_PORT=587
SMTP_FROM=reports@example.com
SMTP_USERNAME=operator-supplied
SMTP_PASSWORD=operator-supplied
SMTP_SECURITY=starttls
```

`starttls` requires STARTTLS; `tls` uses implicit TLS. `none` is intended for a trusted local relay such as the acceptance receiver. No SMTP configuration means the UI shows delivery unavailable. Each member can opt their own account email into one weekly project digest, choosing weekday and hour **in UTC**; the next date is displayed in the browser's timezone. Arbitrary recipients are rejected. Digests contain stored audit evidence and recent scoped alerts, with no fresh provider/model requests. Claims are durable and deduplicated by scheduled period. Delivery history exposes errors; there is no automatic resend after an ambiguous attempt.

## Reports and PDF

The Reports page generates five saved HTML report kinds: `audit`, `rank`, `keywords`, `links`, `ai`. Optional title/byline/accent provide simple branding. Generation preserves source, timestamp, null and sample-limit metadata, escapes evidence HTML, and does not share automatically or fetch fresh data. Rank/keyword samples are capped at 200 rows; link snapshots and AI runs at 100. Audit reports use the latest matching completed audit. Oversized evidence is rejected explicitly.

Enable the renderer profile and set `RENDERER_URL=http://renderer:8080` for **Download PDF**. Chromium runs in a separate restricted renderer service; PDF export disables JavaScript and external network requests, allows embedded data images/inline styles, limits input to 500 KiB and output to 16 MiB, and closes the browser before returning. It does not load external report assets. Existing HTML sharing and revocation rules remain in force.

MCP adds `list_alerts`, `get_alert_settings` and `generate_report`, using the same authorization/domain services as REST. Destination secrets, account deletion and email enrollment are explicit UI/REST operations.

## Business workspace

The Business tab stores a source-labelled profile and review/question/update records, including response drafts. Admin writes use revision checks; members can read. These are **local records and drafts**, not Google Business Profile publishing or sent replies. Up to 1,000 records per project are supported with pagination.

Optional `GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY` enables an explicit read-only Google Place Details preview by exact Place ID. Enable Places API (New) in the operator's Google project and review its billing/field pricing. Responses are transient, not copied into saved records; optional ratings/reviews are a provider-selected sample of up to five. See Google's [Place Details documentation](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/place-details). Live credentials and external publishing are not required for the manual workspace.

## Account deletion

Open **Account**, enter the current password and `DELETE MY ACCOUNT` to request deletion after seven days. Only an authenticated password session can request/cancel; API keys and no-auth mode cannot. The account remains usable and cancellation is available during the grace period. The worker performs due deletion. A sole owner of a shared workspace must first transfer ownership; the worker checks again before purging and reports a blocked reason if ownership changed.

Deletion removes the user, sessions/private records and solo-owned workspaces. Shared workspaces and their project evidence survive; the deleted user's GSC, GA4 and Bing connections are removed. This is application data deletion, not erasure from historical operator backups. Restore procedures must account for deletion requests made after a backup.

## Backup and restore

Python 3.11+ and Docker CLI are required. Choose a new private backup folder outside the repository, with an existing parent:

```powershell
python scripts/maintenance.py backup --container seoseo-db-1 --directory F:/private-backups/seoseo-20261115 --env-file .env
```

The custom-format Postgres dump, operator environment and SHA-256 manifest include encrypted tokens **and the secrets needed to decrypt them**. The script restricts folder/file permissions (including Windows ACL inheritance). Keep the folder private and copy it to secure operator storage. PostgreSQL is durable state; Valkey caches are disposable. Keep matching application images/source and restore the original `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.

Provision an empty target database and choose a new environment output path. Stop application writers on the target before restoration:

```powershell
python scripts/maintenance.py restore --container seoseo-db-1 --db-name seoseo_restored --directory F:/private-backups/seoseo-20261115 --env-output F:/private-backups/restored.env --confirm "RESTORE EMPTY DATABASE"
```

Checksums are checked before restoration; nonempty databases and existing environment output files are refused. `pg_restore` uses one transaction. Review restored database/container addresses, then start matching images/migrations. Retain and periodically test private backups; the script does not configure storage retention or an unattended schedule.

## Acceptance evidence

All checks used disposable data/receivers, without production email, Slack/Discord messages or live Places requests:

- 106 Rust unit tests and doc tests passed; domain tests and workspace clippy with warnings denied were rechecked after report presentation changes.
- Frontend lint/typecheck and production Docker web build passed. Desktop and 390px browser flows passed without page errors or horizontal page overflow: settings, destination test/status, weekly subscription, rank evidence, business profile/review edit with rating preservation, Places preview, report generation/PDF, deletion/cancellation.
- `scripts/e2e-m7.py` passed tenant/member/CAS checks, comparable/incomparable evidence, concurrent evaluation deduplication, actual local webhook delivery, 429/disconnect/redirect refusal without retries, queued destination cancellation, ambiguous-attempt failure without replay, test rate limits, all five reports and escaped HTML. The three added MCP tools passed parity and project isolation checks.
- Real Chromium export passed, including script/external-image isolation. Exported pages were rendered with Poppler and visually inspected.
- A due weekly schedule delivered actual SMTP mail to Mailpit once across worker restarts. Unsubscription was verified. Earlier real local Ollama acceptance satisfies the assistant half of the roadmap exit criterion.
- Seven-day request/cancel and forced-due synthetic purge passed, preserving a shared workspace while deleting a solo workspace/user and its shared-project OAuth grant.
- Real `pg_dump`/empty-target `pg_restore` passed, comparing restored table counts and environment bytes; restoration to a nonempty database was refused.
- Fourteen portable skills validate against all 121 MCP tools.
- Production backend, web and renderer Docker images built successfully. The complete backend acceptance suite passed again with the distroless production API/worker image in the disposable stack; normal Compose configuration also validates.

Reproduce against `deploy/compose.m7check.yaml` (never a production database): build `app` in the documented Rust helper volume, start the disposable stack, run `python scripts/e2e-m7.py`, then `scripts/e2e-m7-browser.cjs` with `PUPPETEER_MODULE` pointing to an installed Puppeteer Core and arguments for web origin, disposable DB container and screenshot folder. Existing assistant fixture/real Ollama commands are in the prior guides. The backend script uses only containers named `seoseo-m7check*`.

Production-image backend QA artifacts are in `F:/seoseo-m7-qa/seoseo-m7-acceptance-o60ch7ah`; browser screenshots and the verified downloaded PDF are in `F:/seoseo-m7-qa/browser/qa-m7-packaged`. The final browser pass also verifies the visible Places rating and source links. Earlier artifacts remain in Windows temp and `F:/seoseo-m7-qa/browser/qa-m7-complete`. These were moved off the system drive after it filled during the first production backend image build attempt. Docker and normal local services recovered without deleting durable volumes; the subsequent production backend image build passed. Backups contain disposable fixture secrets and are not committed. Production deployment is separate from the disposable acceptance stack. Live SMTP/Slack/Discord/Places operator setup remains deployment-specific. M5's live-cloud acceptance and M6's final export closeout remain separate open gates; M7 completion does not close them.

title: M8 â€” Public tools, evidence extras and release packaging

# M8 â€” Public tools, evidence extras and release packaging

M8 implementation adds eleven public tools at `/tools`, a project **Extras** page, a public documentation site at `/docs`, English/Indonesian navigation, optional diagnostics, and multi-architecture release automation. The MCP server exposes **124 tools** including `show_serp_widget`, `show_gsc_widget` and `get_serp_volatility`.

## Public tools

No account or paid key is needed. `POST /api/v1/public/tools` accepts `{tool, content, url}`; maximum content is 256 KiB. Results carry source and limitations. Submitted content is parsed and discarded, never executed or saved.

| Tool | Behavior and evidence boundary |
|---|---|
| `keywords` | Twelve local seed templates. Ideas are brainstorming prompts; no invented search demand. |
| `serp-preview` | Extract title/description from supplied HTML and display a snippet preview. Engines may rewrite snippets. |
| `backlinks` | Extract absolute links to the target host from one supplied source page. No exhaustive backlink index or live freshness claim. |
| `authority` | Read imported Common Crawl SeoSeo Rank; null outside the loaded sample. SR is not Moz DA or Ahrefs DR. |
| `domain-age` | Existing IANA-discovered guarded RDAP lookup, minimal public registry metadata, daily cache. No contacts retained. |
| `robots` | Test supplied rules for SeoSeoBot against the entered URL. Invalid directives may be ignored by the parser. |
| `sitemap` | Check complete XML syntax, root and absolute public locations. Does not crawl locations or validate the full XSD. |
| `meta` | Extract title, description, canonical and robots from supplied HTML. Counts are editorial hints. |
| `schema` | JSON-LD syntax/basic shape and typed-node checks. Not a full Schema.org vocabulary or rich-result eligibility validator. |
| `redirects` | Explicit bounded live HTTP header check. Guarded DNS, robots rules/delay, five redirects, same-origin only; stop at blocks/challenges. No HTML or JavaScript execution. |
| `hreflang` | Extract alternates, duplicate-language hints and resolvable targets from supplied HTML. Reciprocal links and target indexability remain unverified. |

Two fixed Postgres budget rows are shared across replicas: 120 analysis requests and 10 network requests per minute, across the whole instance. No IP fingerprints are stored. Failed validation consumes its budget. Operators exposing these tools publicly should also apply their normal ingress limits.

## Log analysis

`/projects/{project_id}/log-analyses` supports list/create and `/{analysis_id}` deletion. Members read; admins create/delete. Accept Apache/Nginx common or combined format, at most 1 MiB and 20,000 lines. Unsupported/malformed lines are counted as rejected, never guessed. Response bytes of `-` remain unknown.

Only aggregates persist: status counts, recognized self-declared bot-family counts, accepted/rejected lines, known response bytes and unknown-byte rows. Raw logs, IPs, accounts, request paths, query strings, referrers and raw user agents are discarded. Bot names are not verified bot identities. A project lock enforces a rolling maximum of 20 summaries. Exports contain the same aggregates.

## Volatility

`GET /projects/{project_id}/volatility` and `get_serp_volatility` report two distinct measures:

- `index`: mean percentage of replaced top-ten URLs for up to 500 saved keywords in the current project market. Use the latest exact-engine snapshot and its latest same-provider/exactness baseline; current snapshot age and pair gap are limited to 30 days. Both lists must contain ten distinct URLs. Twenty percent means two of ten URLs changed, irrespective of order. This is URL churn, not a Google algorithm-update detector.
- `rank_movement_index`: mean normalized absolute tracked position movement in the latest compatible completed run pair per current-market tracker. Provider, exactness and depth must agree. Measured absence is depth + 1; unchecked rows are excluded.

No evidence means null. Snapshot IDs, coverage and per-keyword churn are exposed for review. Changing the project's market/website excludes unrelated trackers. These are samples of the instance's observations, never a web-wide volatility claim.

## Signed merchant crawler access

Project admins can save/remove the three Web Bot Auth headers on Extras, or use `/projects/{project_id}/crawler-credential`. Use the values generated in **Shopify Admin â†’ Online Store â†’ Preferences â†’ Crawler access**, including the quoted `Signature-Agent` value. Provide the store signature's actual expiry.

The exact credential host must match the project website. Values are single-line and size-bounded; the signature input must cover authority and signature agent and identify Web Bot Auth. Values are AES-GCM encrypted using `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`; GET returns only configured/host/expiry. The worker loads credentials per audit and attaches them only to that exact HTTPS host on port 443, before expiry. Other hosts, subdomains, HTTP downgrades and custom ports never receive them. Changing the project website disables old-host use. Removing a credential prevents new audits from loading it; an already-running audit retains its loaded credential until expiry or completion. Stop that audit for immediate removal from active use.

Robots rules, honest user agent and existing block/rate-limit behavior remain in force. The renderer never receives signed headers; this delivery covers HTTP crawling, not authenticated browser rendering. Shopify verifies the actual signature; saving headers locally does not establish provider acceptance.

Primary provider instructions: [Shopify crawling your store](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/promoting-marketing/seo/crawling-your-store).

## Google Ads CPC (explicit BYOK)

Extras calls `POST /projects/{project_id}/keyword-cpc` only on an administrator's explicit action. Pass 1â€“50 keywords, Google geo target/language constant IDs and expected account currency. The service refreshes an operator-supplied token, reads the actual account currency, then requests historical metrics from fixed Google endpoints. Currency mismatches stop collection. Int64 micros/search counts are parsed without manufacturing zeros; close variants can share a result. Advertising competition is separate from organic keyword difficulty.

Set operator configuration on the API service:

```text
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=...
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=...
GOOGLE_ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN=...
GOOGLE_ADS_CUSTOMER_ID=1234567890
GOOGLE_ADS_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID=... # optional manager account, digits only
GOOGLE_ADS_REFRESH_TOKEN=...     # OAuth grant with adwords scope
GOOGLE_ADS_API_VERSION=v25
```

These are environment secrets, not UI-visible provider keys. The Ads refresh grant is distinct from saved per-project Search Console grants. No Ads credentials means `available:false`, with null CPC/competition/search counts. Errors contain sanitized HTTP status, not provider response bodies or secrets. Results are returned for review/download and not persisted as general SEO metrics.

Primary API contract: [Google historical metrics](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/keyword-planning/generate-historical-metrics).

## MCP Apps

Both widget tools declare `_meta.ui.resourceUri = ui://seoseo/evidence.html`. Authenticated `resources/list` and `resources/read` return a static `text/html;profile=mcp-app` resource. The server advertises the UI extension. SERP widgets use the existing cache-first service and project market; GSC widgets read at most 100 query rows from the selected project property. Existing domain authorization and provider requirements apply.

Every successful widget call returns both structured content and meaningful JSON text. Hosts without Apps support can consume the JSON. The resource speaks the `ui/initialize` / initialized / tool-result protocol through the parent bridge, checks message source, pins the host origin after handshake, filters/reverses the displayed sample locally, and renders values with `textContent`. It requests no network domains or extra permissions. No browser credentials or project data are baked into the HTML.

Protocol: [MCP Apps specification](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/blob/main/specification/2026-01-26/apps.mdx).

## Language and documentation

The English/Indonesian picker persists a device-local preference and updates document language. Navigation, project tabs, tool names and core tool/action labels use the dictionary. Number/date formatting uses the selected locale. Legacy feature prose, provider errors and documentation remain English; this is localization infrastructure and a scoped first dictionary, not a claim that every screen is translated. No new translation library or URL routing scheme is required to extend the dictionary.

`python scripts/build-docs.py` packages canonical `docs/*.md` into the checked-in web bundle. `/docs` lists all guides; `/docs/{filename-without-md}` renders text, headings, tables, code and safe links without executing Markdown HTML. CI runs `--check` to prevent stale documentation. The bundle is self-contained for the existing frontend Docker context.

## Optional diagnostics

`/settings/diagnostics` is restricted to instance administrators using a browser session. Diagnostics are off by default and never scheduled. An administrator can opt in, review the exact payload and send once to an operator-configured public HTTPS `TELEMETRY_URL`. Payload fields are only `schema`, `product` and `version`. The receiver also sees the server IP. No built-in receiver, instance identifier, usage counts, project/account data or automatic retries are included. Turning off prevents subsequent sends. Normal Prometheus operational metrics are independent.

## Release packaging and gates

`.github/workflows/release.yml` reuses the complete CI workflow before publishing backend/frontend images to `ghcr.io/<owner>/<repository>-{backend,frontend}:<tag>`. It runs on version tags or manual dispatch, validates semantic version-shaped tags, builds `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`, and includes provenance and SBOM attestations. Renderer is an optional separately built profile and is not included in the two published core image tags. The registry token is GitHub Actions' package-scoped token, never a local checked-in credential.

After publication, use the existing `SEOSEO_BACKEND_IMAGE` and `SEOSEO_WEB_IMAGE` variables and start Compose without `--build`. Preserve the current images and database backup before upgrading. Migration 0022 is additive; do not modify previously applied migrations.

**Release publication is still open:** no v1.0 tag, GitHub release, GHCR publish or ARM64 image run was performed in this local delivery. A workflow file is not proof of published images. M5's three-live-engine gate and M6's final export gate remain separately documented in the roadmap; M8 does not silently close them. Live Google Ads and merchant Shopify acceptance require their respective credentials and are not established by local checks.

## Acceptance (2026-11-15)

- Rust formatting, Clippy with warnings denied, and all 113 workspace unit tests plus doc tests pass. New tests cover exact-host/HTTPS/port/expiry credential isolation, parser bounds, private targets, PII-free log aggregation, measured absence, complete-list SERP churn and CPC null/close-variant decoding.
- `scripts/e2e-m8.py` passed on `deploy/compose.m8check.yaml`: anonymous tools, private-network denial, input limits, tenant/role/CSRF enforcement, 20-summary retention, deletion, encrypted/redacted/revocable credentials, known 20-percent SERP churn, incomplete-list unknowns, unconfigured CPC, diagnostics defaults/admin policy, and 124-tool MCP resource/structured/JSON behavior.
- `scripts/e2e-m8-browser.cjs` passed on desktop and 390px mobile: anonymous tools and snippet preview, public docs/tables, log submission, CPC unknowns, persistent language selection, no page errors/overflow, and sandbox-host widget handshake/filter/XSS isolation. Screenshots were visually inspected.
- Live public checks returned measured registration metadata from Verisign RDAP for example.com and a robots-aware HTTP 200 redirect-tool result for https://example.com/.
- Frontend lint, typecheck, optimized build and Docker web build pass. The disposable Compose API/worker/web/database/cache stack starts successfully, including migration 0022. The normal instance and its data were not upgraded.

Reproduce after building the debug app in `seoseo-target`:

```bash
docker compose -f deploy/compose.m8check.yaml up -d --build
python scripts/e2e-m8.py
npm ci --prefix renderer
node scripts/e2e-m8-browser.cjs http://localhost:3600 /absolute/path/to/screenshots
python scripts/build-docs.py --check
```

The browser script uses installed Chrome on Windows by default; set `CHROME_PATH` for other environments. The stack is deliberately isolated and contains only disposable test accounts. No tests send paid requests or actual telemetry.
